Routing

Street routing and traffic

5 min readSource

On this page

Coordinate network attachmentAuthorized endpoint accessNames for coordinate pointsSupplied traffic

A City built with OSM supports Walk and Drive variants of Route and Matrix, plus directed walking access for transit. Walk uses the directed pedestrian graph; Drive uses the directed road graph with free-flow time unless the request supplies traffic weights or closures. VIGO never replaces a missing street path with a straight line.

Street Route needs coordinate endpoints and returns full geometry. Street Matrix returns scalar distance and duration per pair without reconstructing every path; it sweeps from the smaller endpoint set, and many-to-one requests use the reverse directed CCH metric while keeping each endpoint's access permissions.

Coordinate network attachment

A free coordinate first attaches to its nearest pedestrian vertex or reciprocal edge. If that attachment belongs to a component with no public transit-access anchor, the query can recover to the nearest anchored component within 80 m. This applies to arbitrary coordinates without place-name exceptions. The connector and partial-edge distance count toward walking time and limits, and returned geometry includes the charged connector. Anonymous Reach seeds use the same recovery.

Drive attaches a free coordinate to the nearest point of a drivable road segment and enters or leaves that road mid-segment, in its own direction. The straight gap is a walk at walking speed, returned as its own walk leg and counted against maxWalkKm. A point with no drivable road within that limit is blocked instead of being driven across open ground. Roads within 25 m of the nearest remain alternatives, which keeps both carriageways of a divided road available, and a nearest road detached from the main road network cannot trap a trip. Traffic closures make a road impassable; they do not move the point to another road.

Stops keep their prepared physical anchors. Recovery never adds a street edge or a stop-to-stop transfer between disconnected components, a mapped authorized terminal path takes precedence, and a restricted endpoint cannot use recovery to bypass its directed exit. An off-network connector is a modeling assumption, not evidence of a surveyed entrance or a barrier-free crossing; an isolated place with no eligible street inside the radius stays unreachable.

Authorized endpoint access

An ordinary movable gate with no access restriction inherits the mapped walking way's permission. Explicit private or prohibited access, locked gates, and unresolved opening times remain excluded. An explicitly walkable platform area can connect two or more mapped walking paths when they share its OSM node IDs. These connections follow the platform boundary; isolated outlines stay excluded. Neither rule invents links across railway tracks or between nearby coordinates. Rebuild a City from its source OSM to apply corrected gate permissions; existing Cities remain readable with their original prepared graph.

Builds default to public pedestrian access: access=private without a pedestrian permission, or foot=private, stays outside the public walking graph. For a population authorized to use internal roads at its own homes and destinations, build with --private-access=endpoints. In Studio, choose City → Street network → Pedestrian access → Authorized endpoints before adding or replacing the OSM PBF; choosing Public paths only and replacing the streets removes the overlay.

This City-wide modeling assumption permits mapped private streets only within the origin's or destination's attached internal street region. An exact directed search follows those streets and interior public islands up to the first public component with a transit-access anchor. The public middle of the journey and stop-to-stop transfers never enter private streets, all internal walking counts toward the same walking limit, and geometry follows the mapped edges. Walking wholly within one internal region is supported.

Destination-only gates (access=destination or foot=destination) are permitted for authorized endpoint access, while locked gates, pedestrian prohibitions, and unresolved opening hours remain excluded. A closer private attachment with no directed public exit does not erase an existing public attachment; a walking-budget cutoff alone cannot trigger this fallback.

The private graph is stored separately, so public street queries are unaffected. network.json records the access model, and transit diagnostics report walkingAccessPermission: "authorized_endpoints". The option assumes endpoint authorization; it does not infer parcel ownership, gate hours, or missing OSM links. Explicit pedestrian prohibitions stay excluded, gates marked prohibited, locked, or with unresolved opening times gain no connections, and Street Reach follows the same rules at the origin and at reached destinations. Rebuild older Cities to apply street-store schema v6, which also excludes isolated platform area outlines from the linear walking graph.

Names for coordinate points

Studio map clicks can use local street names, intersections, named areas or nearby stops instead of a generic pin label. Names are descriptive: they do not move the coordinate or change routing. The optional place_streets and place_areas tables are written during OSM import and ignored by older readers. Cities without those tables fall back to stop names. Reimport OSM to add street names to an older City.

Lookup runs in Rust off the API event loop. A click waits at most 250 ms, then keeps its fallback label; clicks retain their order and pending results are discarded when changing City. Named closed ways are supported for areas; multipolygon area names are not yet included.

Supplied traffic

No traffic provider is connected by default. OSM supplies the baseline road graph and free-flow estimates, and live transit feeds are not a road-speed model. Driving results without an applied traffic snapshot must not be described as current traffic estimates.

Drive Route and Drive Matrix accept a top-level traffic object with routingDataMode: "realtime". A snapshot customizes the prepared directed road graph for one query: a fixed set of edge costs, not a forecast that evolves as a vehicle moves.

JSON
{
  "routingDataMode": "realtime",
  "traffic": {
    "source": "your-provider",
    "observedAt": "2026-09-26T12:00:00Z",
    "ttlSeconds": 300,
    "observations": [
      {
        "fromCoordinate": [-71.0625, 42.3570],
        "toCoordinate": [-71.0615, 42.3575],
        "speedKph": 12
      }
    ]
  }
}

Use the actual observation time and the geometry of an observed directed road path. This fragment shows the schema; its values are illustrative. A full request also needs the mode and endpoints.

ContractBehavior
TimeRequired observation time; validity defaults to 300 seconds and is at most 1,800; observations more than 60 seconds in the future are rejected
ExpiryExpired observations produce an explicit stale_fallback and use baseline costs
GeometryEndpoint pairs or 2–512 coordinates; connected directed path matching within 120 m by default, at most 1,000 m; ambiguous paths are rejected
Edge indicesRequire the exact current streetSourceFingerprint; indices are not portable between street builds
CostsTravel time, speed, or a slowdown factor, plus closures; costs never become faster than the baseline
OverlapConflicting observations on one edge use the largest cost, including closures
ReuseThe customized metric is reused while effective edge updates are unchanged; source age is checked on every query

Read meta.traffic.status in public results (or diagnostics.traffic.status in the internal trace), the matched and unmatched counts, and weightModel. Only applied establishes that supplied costs changed the model; no_matches and free_flow_equivalent do not establish current coverage. The Rust matcher checks connectivity, direction, geometry, length and ambiguity; provider-to-OSM road identity still requires coverage validation, and VIGO does not yet model every turn, signal, intersection delay, parking, or a future traffic trajectory. The traffic input reference lists every effect, expiry rule and limit, plus the Rust-native NDW DATEX II v3 import command.

Routing

Travel-time uncertainty

2 min readSource

On this page

Use reserves in a routing requestCalibrate probabilities before offering themReproduce the implemented contract

VIGO supports explicit time reserves that change which journey is chosen. It does not yet estimate an on-time probability, a travel-time distribution, or a calibrated confidence interval: scheduled and admitted realtime event times are point estimates.

Use reserves in a routing request

ControlApplies toMeaning
minimumTransferBufferMinutesTransit Route and Matrix, depart-at or arrive-byExtra minutes before each subsequent boarding, after walking and published transfer minimums
arrivalBufferMinutesArrive-by transit Route and MatrixReserve the final minutes before the deadline and search for the latest departure that still arrives before the earlier planning deadline

Both are integers from 0 to 60 and default to zero. A positive arrival reserve needs a deadline at least as large as the reserve and a horizon exceeding it by at least one minute; the earliest departure stays the one implied by the original deadline and horizon. Transit via points reject a positive reserve because composing segments would apply it repeatedly, and Walk, Drive, Reach, and native operations reject a positive arrival reserve.

For Harvard Square to South Station, save reserved-arrival.json:

JSON
{
  "origin": {"coordinate": [-71.11902, 42.37334]},
  "destination": {"coordinate": [-71.05524, 42.35227]},
  "serviceDate": "2026-10-05",
  "time": "09:00",
  "timePreference": "arrive_by",
  "maxTransfers": 3,
  "horizonMinutes": 120,
  "minimumTransferBufferMinutes": 3,
  "arrivalBufferMinutes": 5
}
Shell
vigo route --city ./boston --request reserved-arrival.json

VIGO plans arrival by 08:55, allows departure no earlier than 07:00, and requires three extra minutes at each change. These numbers are illustrative preferences, not an MBTA delay estimate or a recommended threshold, and a tighter request can legitimately find no journey.

Route clocks and leg durations still describe the chosen timetable journey, and a Matrix scalar duration keeps its deadline-minus-departure definition, including the reserve. Keep diagnostics.timeReserves with the answer: it records the requested and planning deadlines, both margins, and calibratedProbability: false. Request diagnostics: "trace" to see it. A transfer reserve can absorb some lateness, but it does not model early departures, missed-connection recovery, capacity denial, cancellations, correlated delays, or uncertain walking and station access, and the final reserve alone does not protect intermediate transfers.

Calibrate probabilities before offering them

GTFS-realtime StopTimeEvent.uncertainty has no defined statistical meaning, and an omitted value means unknown. It must not become a standard deviation or a 90% interval without a validated, provider-specific model. See the GTFS realtime reference.

For a Boston calibration study, start with the MBTA LAMP exports and their data dictionary and TransitMatters Gobble. These are potential inputs; VIGO does not download or fit them. A credible next stage would retain historical forecasts and outcomes, match the exact feed revision and trip instance, estimate errors by route, direction, time of day, and lead time, and validate on later dates with coverage reporting. Same-vehicle and shared-corridor delays are correlated, so multiplying marginal transfer probabilities is not a journey probability. Probability-driven routing would need its own search and calibration contract.

Reproduce the implemented contract

Run node test/check-arrive-by-boundary.mjs after building the native kernel and npm run check:standalone after building the compiler. The public fixtures cover a changed selected departure, the exact reserve boundary, blocked outcomes, unchanged earliest departure, transfer-reserve combinations, matrices, invalid values, and repeated requests through both runtimes. They establish modeled feasibility, not measured on-time performance.

Routing

Published fares on itineraries

2 min readSource

On this page

Data and matchingPerformanceVerification

Route shows boarding prices from the imported GTFS feed. In Studio, expand the fare line for ticket names, payment methods, and the agency's fare link; JSON Results carry the same data in each transit leg's fare.

These are prices for a new boarding, not an optimized journey fare. Multi-leg results deliberately have no total, because joining legs, transfer discounts, passes, and existing tickets can change what a rider pays. A missing quote does not mean free travel, and path selection does not consider price.

Data and matching

The importer keeps fare tables and their route, station, agency, and calendar references in an optional fare_catalogs SQLite table. Catalogs travel with a City and stay separate when feeds are merged. Cities built before fares were added need their original GTFS reimported to keep fare data.

  • Fares v2 takes precedence when fare_products.txt is present. Matching uses route networks, station areas, rule priorities, fare timeframes, and the default rider category; product names and media come from the feed. MBTA's transfer_only extension is honored, so a free-transfer product never becomes a free new boarding.
  • Fares v1 supports flat, route, and origin/destination-zone boarding prices. Zone-traversal (contains_id) rules stay unquoted.
  • Fare timeframes use the civil date and time at the validation stop, including its timezone, daylight-saving changes, times after midnight, and calendar exceptions. For a realtime-adjusted leg, the original scheduled stop sequence must be uniquely recoverable before timed rules apply.
  • Explicit platform fare areas override inherited station areas. Ambiguous network assignments, conflicting products, missing references, and unsupported conditions stay unquoted, and an unreadable fare catalog never discards a computed route.
  • Transfer totals, joined fare legs, pass selection, non-default rider eligibility, and fare-based optimization are not implemented.

Matching follows the GTFS Schedule reference. No agency prices or route-name rules are embedded in code; prices reflect the saved feed.

Performance

Fare lookup happens only after route selection, so no fare code runs inside routing, matrix, or Reach searches. Catalogs load by feed scope and are indexed once; quote, candidate, catalog, and scheduled-trip caches have explicit bounds and are released with their catalog. With cached catalogs, annotation performs no SQL. First-use parsing, serialization, and rendering still take time; measure them separately with node scripts/benchmark-fares.mjs FEED.zip STORE.sqlite YYYY-MM-DD report.json.

Verification

node test/check-gtfs-fares.mjs covers exact matching, missing data, published zero fares, invalid prices, transfer-only products, default rider categories, area inheritance, empty-rule semantics, priority rules, after-midnight date changes, time-window boundaries, scoped multi-feed import and merge, and non-mutating itinerary annotation.

PreviousTime reservesNextRead a Result
Results

Read a Result

6 min readSource

On this page

Version policyReading a resultJourneyKeep uncertainty with the answerDiagnosticsMatrix and ReachCompare saved resultsKeep a reproducible runDetailed wrapper transport

Version policy

Public v1 schemas preserve required fields, their types, units, and meanings. Removing or renaming a field, changing its units, or changing a status meaning requires a new schema version. Additional optional fields may be introduced; clients should ignore unknown fields. trace, native kernel structures, and Studio's internal worker messages are outside this stability policy. Result schema versions are independent of prepared City formats.

V1 uses the public result schemas; there is no legacy-envelope adapter. See upgrading for the City rebuild and rollback procedure.

Reading a result

The CLI, resident stream, and HTTP services use one public result contract. Read status first: ok contains the result, not_found means no journey satisfies this request, and error means the request failed. A valid no-journey response exits 0 and uses HTTP 200.

Route returns schema: "vigo.route.v1", query, journey, and meta. Matrix and Reach use vigo.matrix.v1 and vigo.reach.v1. The schema version and meta.engineVersion are separate identities.

Interactive Route commands show a short itinerary. Pipes, --output, and --format json produce structured JSON; --format text explicitly selects the terminal view. Diagnostic details are available in JSON.

Journey

journey contains departureTime, arrivalTime, durationSeconds, walkingSeconds, waitingSeconds, ridingSeconds, boardings, transfers, and legs. Drive journeys also have drivingSeconds. Clocks are local service-day HH:MM:SS, including hours above 23. Durations are integer seconds, rounded at the public boundary; routing retains its original precision. Waiting includes the gaps before and between legs. It is not inferred to be a reliability margin.

Legs have type: "walk" | "transit" | "drive", from, to, clocks, duration, and available distance. Transit legs identify the route and trip. Stop, route, and trip references use { "feed": "mbta", "id": "70067" }; an unscoped feed is null. You can send an endpoint as { "stop": { "feed": "mbta", "id": "70067" } }. Older string stopId requests remain accepted.

Route includes available GeoJSON geometry on each leg by default, preserving the full source coordinate precision and vertex sequence. A transit line runs from the boarding stop through the aligned shape vertices to the alighting stop, and its distanceMeters is the length of that line. A walk that starts or ends off the street network reports the short connection as endpointConnector. Send includeGeometry: false or use --include-geometry=false for a smaller response without coordinate arrays. Matrix journey geometry remains opt-in with includeGeometry: true. Geometry describes the modeled path, not an observed vehicle trajectory or a guarantee of surveyed station interiors. Ordered journeys have a single ordered leg list.

Additional journeys appear in alternatives, which excludes the primary journey and duplicates and is omitted when none remain. alternativeSearch describes how they were found. Requested alternative journeys (alternatives, alternativeRanking) are available in both runtimes and report coverage: "requested_time". Standalone journey windows sample later departures or earlier arrival deadlines and report their sampling direction.

With sharedLegs: true, journey.sharedLegAlternatives bundles shared-leg services. Each option retains a full timed journey and identifies the replaced leg by legIndex. Coverage is bounded to one-leg substitutions; options cannot be combined. frequencies reports counts and observed headways from active, path-verified segment departures in an explicit window; these counts are independent of onward-transfer feasibility.

Transit legs carry a fare when the City publishes GTFS Fares v1 or v2 data for the ride. Both runtimes price legs with the same engine.

Keep uncertainty with the answer

quality.streetGeometry distinguishes verified street evidence from unverified geometry. quality.stationPath is source_path or inferred when station access is present. A verified street segment does not certify a complete entrance-to-platform path. components separates street and station access costs and identifies their source types. Transit quality.schedule: "timetable" means modeled timetable times, not observed punctuality or a guarantee that every source timestamp was measured.

Route warnings describe qualifications that affect the returned journey. Dataset/model limitations live in vigo info (Rust), vigo inspect (Node), or GET /v1/info; send includeLimitations: true when needed alongside a query. No warnings does not certify complete source coverage. Unsupported GTFS semantics remain documented in known limits.

Diagnostics

LevelAdded output
none (default)Journey or analysis result only
summaryAvailable integer search counters and candidate counts
profileSummary plus measured timings in integer microseconds
traceProfile plus the full original internal result under trace

Use --diagnostics summary, a JSON diagnostics field, or ?diagnostics=summary. HTTP also accepts ?vigo_diagnostics=summary. Conflicting body and URL settings are rejected. trace is an unstable research/debug ABI: internal indices, sentinels, duplicate units, and raw candidate arrays intentionally remain there. Production clients should consume the public fields.

scannedDepartures is the engine's departure scan count; expandedTripRuns and relaxedStops are its reported expansion/relaxation counts. They are not interchangeable with network size or unique visited stops. Candidate counts count the returned endpoint candidate entries. Fields without instrumentation are omitted rather than fabricated. The Rust and Node runtimes return the same public result for the same request and City; summary and profile fields describe each runtime's own instrumentation and are not comparable across runtimes.

meta.computeUs retains the runtime's measured compute boundary, identified by computeScope: "query_dispatch_including_materialization": service-date activation, search, and result materialization. It excludes public formatting, final JSON serialization, HTTP queueing, and network transit. Profile scopes can overlap and must not be summed. Server-Timing reports measured serialization and compute; the Rust supervisor also reports queue time. Client wall time remains a separate measurement.

meta.requestId identifies a result; caller-supplied id is echoed. meta.queryFingerprint hashes the caller's request, with stop references canonicalized, and the City revision; output switches (id, diagnostics, includeGeometry, includeLimitations, reachFormat) are excluded. The same request has the same fingerprint in both runtimes. Equivalent requests written differently, for example time and timeMinutes, can hash differently. Supplied scenario and realtime content get separate fingerprints; retain the original inputs for reproducibility. Realtime admission/application evidence is retained when the runtime supplies it.

Matrix and Reach

Matrix returns durationsSeconds[origin][destination], with ordered endpoints in query. Unreachable cells are null, never zero. Optional journeys follows the same ordering. Arrive-by duration is the requested deadline minus latest departure; a nested journey can arrive earlier and have a shorter elapsed duration.

Reach returns surface.valuesSeconds, grid bounds and dimensions, cutoffsSeconds, GeoJSON contours/areas, and fullSurface when available. Cell order is unchanged: row-major, northwest first. Unreachable cells remain null. GeoJSON cutoff properties and explicitly requested street/node evidence retain their documented unit-labelled fields; these analytical evidence formats are separate from journey durations. Raw search chains are only in trace.

For a map, request reachFormat: "map". The result contains areas and bounds for the full reached extent, without raster values, stop lists or duplicate contours. Its polygons equal fullAreas in the default reachFormat: "full" response. Use the full response for grid comparisons and request includeNodes or includeEdges only with that format.

Compare saved results

Public saved results can be compared without rerunning routing. Changes are after minus before, in seconds. Route reports duration and transfer changes; Matrix and Reach report common, faster, slower, unchanged, newly reachable and no-longer-reachable counts. Means use only mutually reachable entries and are null when none exist. Matrix requires identical ordered endpoints; Reach requires the same grid. Callers must align other experimental assumptions.

For a source-data audit, request diagnostics: "trace" and retain the original witness under trace. Low-level native operations have a separate field reference.

Keep a reproducible run

Errors use schema: "vigo.error.v1", status: "error", and error.code / error.message. Handle stable codes and HTTP status, not OS error text. Keep the City, original query, executable version, supplied observations/scenario, and result together when retaining a reproducible run.

Untimed GTFS stairs and gates using routing estimates expose quality.stationTime: "estimated" on the walk. Their diagnostic provenance is gtfs_pathway_estimated; these costs are not published or measured traversal times.

Detailed wrapper transport

stream --stream-output=detailed sends a vigo.stream.detail.v1 envelope containing id, status: "ok", and trace, without constructing a second public result. The trace is the same complete internal result provided by --diagnostics=trace; it remains an unstable internal ABI. Envelope ok means execution completed: inspect the detailed result's routing status to distinguish a journey from a valid blocked outcome. Failures retain the standard vigo.error.v1 envelope and do not stop subsequent requests.

Clients must check capabilities.output.streamFormats for detailed before selecting this transport. VIGO-py negotiates it automatically and falls back to the full public trace response on earlier compatible runtimes. The default stream output remains the public result schema.

Results

Walking costs and source evidence

4 min readSource

On this page

Time and connectivity are separatePedestrian permissionsWhat a returned route establishesUpgrade and check

VIGO V1 enforces stop-transfer walking floors, OSM node restrictions, and explicit missing station coordinates. Both Node Engine and standalone Rust use the same prepared City data. Rebuild Cities that predate the supported format from the original GTFS and OSM inputs as described below.

Time and connectivity are separate

A GTFS transfer minimum constrains the time between services. It does not describe a physical path or permit arbitrarily fast walking. Before searching, VIGO prices each expanded stop pair at the larger of the published minimum and its distance divided by the configured walking speed, rounded up to a whole second. The distance is at least the straight-line separation of valid stop coordinates. That separation supplies a lower bound; a missing interior path remains unknown.

GTFS pathways describe directed station connections. An explicit traversal_time remains a source cost, including for lifts and moving walkways. If it is absent, VIGO derives a time from the available length and walking policy. A declared pathway supports the feed's connectivity model; it is not a current field measurement. When a station declares pathways and public entrances, coordinate access uses those entrances; snapping straight to a platform cannot bypass the station connections.

The walking floor enters preparation before boarding selection, so a depart-at query may choose a later connection and an arrive-by query may require an earlier departure. Route and both scalar and journey Matrix modes use those same costs.

Pedestrian permissions

The OSM importer reads tags on ways and their nodes, including packed dense nodes. It excludes foot=no, foot=private, and foot=use_sidepath, honors explicit pedestrian permission over generic access, and preserves directed pedestrian rules. A motor-vehicle one-way restriction alone does not prohibit walking in the reverse direction.

For nodes, impassable barriers and denied access exclude incident pedestrian segments. Ambiguous gates require explicit permission. Foot/access conditional rules and opening hours other than 24/7 are excluded because this static model does not evaluate their conditions. This conservative policy can reduce coverage, including approaches to a blocked barrier. Driving retains its separate permissions. See the OSM definitions of foot access and pedestrian direction.

What a returned route establishes

streetPathVerified concerns the prepared street graph; it is not independent proof of an entire door-to-platform walk. Free-coordinate snapping is returned separately as endpointConnector, with streetPathVerified: false. The walk's line still starts or ends at the requested coordinate, so a journey is drawn without gaps; its first or last segment is that connector. An assumed station interior has stationAccessStatus: "unverified"; a published transfer minimum does not change that status. Selected station costs and stop chains are exposed in accessCost when available.

An independent physical audit needs a continuous, directed source path, legal node/way access, and evidence for the links between the requested location, street, stop, entrance, and platform. A line near an OSM street is insufficient. Source gaps require better mapped entrances, agency pathways, or validated access links. Even complete source evidence does not establish current closures or observed travel times.

An interior GTFS node may omit coordinates. VIGO retains its declared pathway connections and stop ID but omits that node from displayed geometry, setting stationGeometryStatus: "incomplete". A line between the remaining known coordinates is schematic. If a source-timed pathway also lacks length and located endpoints, its distance contributes only a zero lower bound and the leg reports stationDistanceStatus: "lower_bound"; it is not measured zero-distance walking. When traversal_time is absent, stairs with a nonzero stair_count use one second per step and fare/exit gates use five seconds. These fixed routing assumptions are recorded as gtfs_pathway_estimated, retain stationAccessStatus: "unverified", and are floored by available distance at the configured walking pace. They are not measured or agency-published traversal times. Explicit traversal times take precedence. Other pathways without time, length, or distinct located endpoints remain excluded and reported as unpriced_pathways. The declared station topology remains in force, so exclusion cannot create a fallback shortcut. A feed-supplied connection alone does not certify its physical duration.

Upgrade and check

Build a new City with the current runtime and the retained raw GTFS/OSM inputs. Use the Boston quickstart and a new output directory, then open it with the engine as described in the engine manual. Keep the old City with its original runtime for reproducibility.

Street schema v4 cannot be upgraded by reopening a cache: its missing node restrictions require reimport from the original PBF. The current street schema is v6; it also excludes platform area outlines from walking links. Routing-store schema v3 distinguishes missing coordinates and pathway costs from genuine zeros and requires a fresh GTFS import. Transfer semantics v4 additionally requires reimport to recover pathway modes and stair counts discarded by earlier imports. Prepared access policy v9 connects street transfers to public entrances and composes their directed station pathways during preparation and prices travel between projections on the same street segment directly. Each boarding transfer can include at most one external transfer edge; the itinerary retains every original pathway segment. Declared pathways suppress invented parent-station shortcuts. Node Engine refreshes outdated timing preparations; standalone Rust requires current prepared data and rejects stale street, routing-store, or transfer-time policies.

Public regression checks use generated inputs and can be run from the source checkout:

Shell
npm run check:osm-pbf
npm run check:national-focused
npm run check:standalone

These checks exercise node barriers, access overrides, malformed node tags, pedestrian direction, physically feasible transfer selection in both time directions, scalar/journey matrices, and rejection of old prepared data. They test the implementation and declared input model, not the completeness of any agency's pedestrian map.

Known limits

4 min readSource

On this page

GTFSTransit Route and MatrixStreetsRealtimeCity reuse and platformsScenario and Reach

VIGO models the City revision and query it is given. It does not certify real-world service, demand, safety, or operational feasibility.

GTFS

  • Support is limited to the source features listed in GTFS support. Unsupported or malformed features are reported during the build.
  • Missing published shapes do not prevent timetable routing but limit map geometry.
  • Explicit GTFS in-seat links at a shared terminal keep passengers aboard across trip changes. Route, Matrix and Reach count one boarding and preserve onboard layovers. Studio shows “Stay aboard.” Block-based continuation is not inferred, and missing feed links are not guessed. Existing Cities must be rebuilt if their importer discarded those links.
  • Staying aboard must move the rider onward. A Route journey boards a looping vehicle where it passes for the last time, at the boarding stop or at another stop the origin walk reaches in time. Route alternatives and window choices drop a journey that stays aboard through a turnaround and then reaches a stop the rider could already have reached by then, through the same stop or one transfer walk with the transfer buffer, or that would reach the destination no later by leaving before the turnaround. Window choices leave out such a journey while another transit choice remains. The test uses only the journey's own stops and clocks, where the feed lets riders off and on, and the City's stop-to-stop walks; with walks between stops turned off, only same-stop returns count.

Transit Route and Matrix

  • Arrive-by Matrix durations include any wait between actual arrival and the deadline; use Route or Matrix journeys for actual arrival.
  • Transfer and arrival reserves can change route selection, but VIGO does not compute calibrated arrival probabilities or delay distributions.
  • A finite maxTransfers cap with ordered transit waypoints is unsupported.
  • Station returns may be valid in the supplied timetable; they are flagged, not excluded.
  • Without an explicit rule or declared pathway topology, platforms sharing a parent station use a transfer assumption of at least 120 seconds, floored by their coordinate distance at walking speed. These legs report transferSource: 'parent_station_fallback' and schematic geometry, not a verified station pathway.
  • A street route to a platform coordinate does not establish an entrance-to-platform connection. Walks touching subway stops or platforms report stationAccessStatus: 'unverified' unless they carry a declared pathway with no estimated segments; streetSegmentVerified keeps the narrower OSM result. Untimed stairs and gates use explicit routing estimates (one second per step, five seconds per gate), marked gtfs_pathway_estimated. Scalar Matrix results do not carry this per-leg audit.
  • Departure windows sample integral minutes; they are not continuous profiles.

Streets

  • Walk and Drive depend on OSM coverage and directionality.
  • Pedestrian attachment searches vertices within 160 m and projects onto reciprocal edges within 80 m. A missing attachment is not proof that no physical path exists.
  • Platform polygons describe an area, not a walking line. Street-store schema v6 excludes their outlines from the walking graph; routing across polygon interiors is not modeled, and older Cities need a source rebuild.
  • An anonymous endpoint on an unanchored fragment can recover to the nearest transit-connected component within 80 m, including the full connector cost. This adds no graph links and proves nothing about buildings, fences, water, or levels in between. See coordinate attachment.
  • Authorized endpoint access is an opt-in build model; it does not establish individual permissions, gate hours, or missing connections.
  • Drive does not yet model every turn restriction, signal, or intersection delay. Traffic must be supplied by the caller.

Realtime

  • Realtime transit applies to Route only, and only with a supplied realtimeSnapshot and explicit realtime selection. Transit Matrix and Reach reject realtime requests. Vehicle Positions and Alerts do not change route costs or close services.
  • Only FULL_DATASET feeds are decoded. Updates modify matched scheduled trips, remove CANCELED and DELETED trips, and omit SKIPPED calls. Added, duplicated, replacement, and unscheduled trips without a supported scheduled instance are unsupported for routing, though Studio can display them.
  • Feed and record timestamps must pass freshness checks: up to 180 seconds old and 60 seconds ahead of the captured clock. Missing timestamps do not establish freshness. See realtime routing.

City reuse and platforms

  • Copy the entire City directory; street indexes and prepared files are part of it. Executables are specific to an OS and CPU, while City data is portable across the supported 64-bit targets.
  • Older Cities with ephemeral Drive CCH rebuild that hierarchy on fresh-process startup; rebuilding the City from source enables persisted Drive CCH.
  • An incompatible timetable cache, a new active-service pattern, a changed walking policy, or an evicted snapshot requires preparation. Missing or corrupt required street indexes are errors; restore the complete City or rebuild it.
  • Studio project settings, drafts, and live connections are local application state and do not travel inside a City. Studio cannot open compiler City directories in this release.

Scenario and Reach

  • Planned transit service changes apply to Reach; supplied traffic applies to Drive Route and Drive Matrix. Other combinations are rejected.
  • maxTransfers limits changes between vehicles in both baseline and scenario Reach; zero permits one ride, and walking never counts as a boarding.
  • After the last ride, Reach follows the same declared station exits as coordinate egress, and a stop reached only by a transfer walk does not restart the walking allowance. Reach rasterizes reached street edges while Matrix evaluates destination coordinates, so their cells can differ under matching settings.
  • Reach measures modeled travel time, not people, jobs, demand, welfare, observed behavior, or operational feasibility.

Studio

VIGO Studio

6 min readSource

On this page

Documentation and settingsOpen a CityNetworkRoutePlanSave a journeyRecentAnalyzeReachCompareCityData sourcesPreferencesStudio troubleshootingPlayback shows no tripsAn access path crosses a blockA date is rejectedA loading indicator is not advancing

VIGO Studio puts Network, Route, Analyze, and City views over the same routing engine. It keeps its own project library and works offline once a City is imported. See Networks within one City for network selection, timetable quality, and journey choices.

Documentation and settings

Open Settings → Documentation from the City library or the sidebar to read this guide offline, in Studio's light or dark appearance. Press / to search; links to source files and external references open in your browser. Reading documentation does not open a City or prepare routing data, and the API schema download is bundled locally.

Open a City

Select a project from the Studio library and import GTFS and OSM. Rebuild when the source feed or street extract changes. Studio stores projects in its library format and cannot open the movable City directories built by the compiler in this release. Opening a City prepares walking for transit access and walking routes; the driving network opens when you select Drive. Background tasks shows preparation progress.

Network

Use Network for reporting coverage and service events, and Routes for trip times, station boards, and line views. Route and station selection is shared across the tabs. Network and Routes explains playback, live timing, added service, and source freshness.

Route

Plan

Pick an origin and destination on the map. Add point inserts a via point before the destination, up to eight points in total; click a row to repick it, use the arrows to reorder it, or remove it, and Reverse flips the sequence. You can also type a coordinate command in Search VIGO, such as route 38.90, -77.05 to 38.91, -77.03 at 08:00, then choose Plan this journey. The route form does not search place or station names.

Choose a travel mode. Realtime transit departs now; Scheduled exposes the date, time, and depart-at or arrive-by controls. Transfer caps are disabled while via points are present. Changing points or options updates the route, Rerun route submits the same coordinates again, and New route clears them.

Network chooses what a transit route runs on: the City timetable or one of the City's saved scenarios. A scenario route uses the scheduled timetable of the scenario's timetable group, with its removed routes canceled and its planned lines added. Planned lines run on their stated headway and hours on every service date, and new planned stops are reached on foot over the City's streets. Rides on planned service are labeled Planned and drawn along the scenario's path. Realtime is unavailable while a scenario is chosen.

Sort journeys by Earliest, Fewer transfers, or Less walking. Each card shows arrival, total time from your requested departure, transfers, walking, and its trade-off against the earliest arrival. Sorting keeps the selected journey and does not rerun the search; arrow keys, Home, and End select another journey, and Details opens its itinerary.

Save a journey

Choose a format beside Save in the journey details. JSON keeps the selected plan, diagnostics, and a summary separating the initial wait, journey duration, and total elapsed time. Markdown is a readable itinerary whose clocks can exceed 23 hours after service-day midnight. GeoJSON keeps leg geometry and its source when the complete path is retained. CSV records each leg's trip and service-clock times; clock_service_date names the midnight those minutes count from, and minutes can exceed 1440. Saving never reruns the query.

Save all beneath the journey choices keeps every completed alternative, including those beyond the five visible cards. Filenames include the service date, places, and export time.

Recent

Reopen recent Route Results for the current City revision. Each keeps its normalized request, status, warnings, and timing beside the journey.

Analyze

Reach

Choose an origin on the map, or use Choose origin to search imported stops by name or ID or enter coordinates. Run Reach, then switch between Reachable area, Reached streets, and cutoffs; changing the displayed cutoff reuses the retained result. See Reach for limits and bounds.

Choose Arrive by to map where a destination can be reached from by a deadline. The chosen point becomes the destination and the clock its Deadline; each place shows how many minutes before the deadline a traveler must leave it, and the walking limit applies to the first walk. Compare runs the same arrive-by question for every variant.

Compare

Compare measures saved scenarios, timetable groups, or single timetables against one reference, by default the City's Baseline group, from the same origin and departure. Every variant is computed on the reference's grid, and the reference surface is computed once and reused. Variants are ranked by reached area gained at the time budget; each row also counts newly reached and no-longer-reached cells, the mean minutes saved over cells both networks reach, and the change in reached stops. Choose a variant to map its travel-time change from the reference. Cell counts are never subtracted across independent grids. To compare completed Results without rerunning them, use the compiler's compare.

Use Save beside Reach or comparison results for the full JSON, the selected cutoff's area geometry, or a CSV summary; Compare saves its ranking as CSV, the run with the mapped variant as JSON, and the mapped pair's areas as GeoJSON. total_processing_ms measures complete analysis processing, separate from native query timings; area_source distinguishes an exact-cutoff area metric from a display-raster calculation; reference_surface and reference_feed_id identify the baseline. Saving becomes available when the computation finishes.

Studio saves scenarios and timetable groups in the City folder, in .vigo/scenarios.json, shortly after each edit. They survive restarts and reimports and travel with the City directory; a scenario that names a route a reimport removed reports it when you run it. A copy saved from another window is never overwritten: Studio shows the newer copy instead. Drafts that earlier versions kept in the browser profile move into the City folder the first time you open it. For a stop inserted on an A → B edge shared by several branches, the road path applies to each affected branch, and each branch keeps its own untouched shape and runtime. Use the engine, the compiler, or Python for Matrix queries.

City

Data sources

Open City → Data sources to review GTFS feeds, OSM coverage, counts, and warnings. To remove a source, select the trash button beside its row, check the name, and confirm Delete source. Removing a GTFS feed refreshes the combined timetable from the remaining feeds; removing OSM removes street routing and OSM-derived walking transfers until another import. The City, other sources, saved notebooks, and your original files are kept, and deletion is unavailable during import or preparation.

Preferences

Choose appearance, storage location, and map preferences. The default City folder is ~/Documents/Vigo Projects. On macOS, Studio does not scan or test-write the library until you choose Open library folder, when macOS may ask for permission. Locally rebuilt apps use ad-hoc signatures, so an updated build can need authorization again.

Local OSM is the default basemap. It draws main roads, rivers, lakes, and coastal water from the City's imported PBF in light or dark appearance, with no tile service, API key, or network connection; residential streets, paths, buildings, and labels are omitted to keep routes and analysis clear. Cities imported before the local map index need one fresh OSM import. Online OpenStreetMap and CARTO styles remain optional.

Studio troubleshooting

Playback shows no trips

Check the exact service date, calendar.txt, calendar_dates.txt, the selected direction and pattern, and whether the playback time falls between a trip's first departure and last arrival. A route-wide total is not the number of vehicles active at once.

An access path crosses a block

The access or egress line must come from OSM street geometry. Rebuild from current OSM data, confirm the point lies within coverage, and inspect the selected street leg. Studio never replaces a missing street path with a straight jump.

A date is rejected

Use an exact YYYY-MM-DD date inside the feed's active service range. Studio applies the same calendar rules as the command line.

A loading indicator is not advancing

Background tasks show measured bytes or records for steps with a known total; the percentage belongs to that step, not the whole import. Work without a total shows an indeterminate bar, elapsed time, and the age of the last update. If updates pause, use Reconnect to task: the task may still be running, so check its status before importing the same source again. Confirm that the City folder is readable and writable and that macOS has granted access.

Network and Routes

4 min readSource

On this page

Read the evidenceInvestigate a conditionSee what needs attentionInspect a route or stationPatterns and scheduled playbackVehicle timing and line viewAdded serviceVerification and referencesEvidence limits

Open Network in VIGO Studio to inspect the selected City's timetable, live reports, and service events. The workspace has Network and Routes tabs; use Route for journey planning and Analyze for Reach.

Read the evidence

The same map can show several kinds of evidence. Read the source and observation time before interpreting a change.

What you seeWhat it representsHow to use it
Scheduled timeAn indexed GTFS arrival or departure on the selected service dateEstablish the published plan; check the date and pattern
Predicted timeA matched, admitted TripUpdate for that trip and stopCompare the same arrival or departure with its schedule
Vehicle positionA reported location and stop status at its own observation timeLocate the vehicle; check its age separately from the prediction
Estimated playbackA position interpolated along the scheduled tripExplore the timetable and geometry
Service eventComputed delay, spacing change, or source alert with observation timestampsInspect the event evidence and source age

None of these is a verified history of actual stop arrivals, and a missing prediction stays unknown. A vehicle marker or an added trip in Trip times does not mean Route can use that trip; routing has its own admission rules.

Investigate a condition

  1. Start with coverage. Check the snapshot time, feed freshness, and reporting counts in Network. Reporting counts routes with current trip reports; it is not the share of passengers covered or service running on time.
  2. Follow the route. Open Routes, select the route, and inspect Trip times on the relevant date. Use Stops to confirm direction and pattern, then Updates for service evidence.
  3. Inspect the same event. Open the station board or select a vehicle in Line view. Compare arrival with arrival, or departure with departure, at the same stop, keeping both observation times visible.
  4. Keep the observation attached. Export observations or Export report retains the current evidence and source timestamps.

For a journey, use Route and read its Result and diagnostics. Event details retain the scheduled comparison, source timestamps and source references.

See what needs attention

Network shows reporting coverage, route comparisons, and service events. A scheduled departure, a feed prediction, and an observed vehicle location are different evidence, and missing reports remain unknown.

Inspect a route or station

Open Routes and choose a route to see Trip times; select a trip and date to compare scheduled and predicted arrivals or departures. Stops opens directions and patterns, and Updates opens service evidence. The map and Line view show the same route. Select a stop for its arrivals board, and All routes returns to the catalog. Route and station selection is shared across Network, Routes, the map, and the line view; Network map clears both.

Patterns and scheduled playback

A route's Stops view shows directions, patterns, ordered stops, service span, and published geometry. Patterns are labeled by first and last stops, and Full service restores them all. Direction IDs 0 and 1 are feed labels, not compass directions. Technical IDs appear under Source data. Times such as 25:10 stay on their GTFS service day.

Scheduled playback is labeled Estimated: vehicles dwell at stops and follow their pattern's shape between timed calls. The index does not keep shape_dist_traveled or every untimed call, so interpolated positions are not exact. Live positions stay separate from playback, and route-colored vehicle circles show a bearing arrow when available.

Vehicle timing and line view

In Network → Routes, select a route and choose Line view. The two tracks show each direction's stops and reported vehicles. Select a vehicle on the map or the line to compare scheduled and predicted arrival and departure at its reported stop. If that stop has no usable timing, its prediction stays unavailable; Next prediction names a later stop with one without substituting its time.

Vehicle timing comes from the City's connection store and the current realtime snapshot. The browser requests only the selected route or vehicle every ten seconds, without overlapping requests.

  • Stop placement follows the VehiclePosition stop ID, sequence, and status; it never uses road snapping or interpolated movement. Missing or conflicting identities stay unplaced.
  • Arrival comes from the incoming connection and departure from the outgoing one, and delay compares the same event at the same stop.
  • Opposite directions share a central station list only when their station sequences are exact reverses. Bus stops on opposite sides of a street are not paired by proximity or name.
  • Branches and repeated stops stay distinct. Skipped stops, missing predictions, duplicates, and stale observations never become valid current timing.

Spacing is schematic: it shows stop order, not distance, time, or headway. The ↔ warning marks both vehicles in a compressed departure pair, comparing their predictions at the same stop against their scheduled interval.

Added service

Trips declared by GTFS-RT ADDED or NEW appear in the line view and the Trip times selector even when absent from the static timetable. Their reported stop sequences supply placement and timing; partial sequences are labeled as reported stops, and scheduled times and delay comparisons are unavailable. Added-service display does not make a trip available to journey routing; see realtime limits.

Verification and references

test/check-agency-route-line.mjs and test/check-added-service-display.mjs run with npm run check:agency. They cover both directions, branches, repeated and terminal stops, conflicting sequences, stale and future positions, skipped and no-data predictions, and added trips; they verify fixture behavior, not field accuracy. The interaction design drew on TransitMatters Train Tracker and Swiftly's Live Operations overview; no implementation or assets were copied. Matching follows the GTFS Realtime reference.

Evidence limits

Predicted spacing is not measured headway, and retained forecast changes are not actual vehicle progression. Reporting coverage is not service health. Network inspection does not establish delay causes, recovery forecasts or passenger impacts. VIGO does not dispatch vehicles or publish messages.

Engine and HTTP API

The VIGO engine

1 min readSource

VIGO 1.0.0-rc.2 · CLI and HTTP reference · Prepared City format 1

VIGO runs routing and isochrone queries from a single Rust executable. The executable contains the routing kernels, City loader, JSON interface, and HTTP server. It needs no Node, Python, browser, external routing service, or internet connection at query time. SQLite is compiled in. City data is supplied separately and opened read-only.

This manual describes the standalone Rust interface. Requests retain vigo.standalone.query.v1; public results share vigo.route.v1, vigo.matrix.v1, and vigo.reach.v1 with the Node CLI. Studio and the private Python worker protocol remain separate. Run vigo capabilities to identify the executable before integrating it.

  • Command lineCommands, flags, files, and standard input.
  • Requests and fieldsPoints, clocks, units, and the fields every query shares.
  • RouteJourneys, alternatives, via points, and departure windows.
  • MatrixTravel times for many origins and destinations in one request.
  • ReachRasters, polygons, contours, and street evidence.
  • HTTP APIEndpoints, limits, status codes, and authentication.
  • Output and errorsPublic results, trace output, and diagnostics.
  • Native operationsPacked-array kernel calls and their field reference.

This manual is also part of the searchable, offline VIGO guide, which the engine serves at /. The OpenAPI specification contains the HTTP request contracts and native input/output types. The audit record describes tested coverage and remaining boundaries.

Engine and HTTP API

Engine command line

3 min readSource

On this page

CommandsQuery flagsFiles and standard input

Use the command line to inspect a City, run a query, or start a service.

Commands

All paths are local filesystem paths. Every data command requires --city DIR or VIGO_CITY; this includes compare. Help, version, and capabilities need no City.

CommandPurposeMain input
help, --help, -hPrint the command overviewNone
version, --version, -VPrint version and runtimeNone
capabilitiesSupported operations and compatibility flagsNone
infoLoaded City identity and summariesCity
routeOne origin–destination route, optionally via/windowJSON or endpoint flags
matrixAll origin–destination travel timesJSON arrays
reach, isochroneReachable streets, raster, polygons, isolinesJSON or origin flags
compareChanges between two saved Reach resultsJSON with before and after
nativeLow-level Rust operationsoperation and typed input
streamResident NDJSON request/response processOne JSON object per stdin line
serveResident HTTP serviceCity and server flags
healthCheck a running service's readiness without loading a City--host, --port

Use vigo route --help for the general command overview. --name value and --name=value both work. Unknown options, irrelevant options, repeated options, and extra positional arguments fail. Boolean flags are bare for true or use --pretty=false; --pretty false is not the boolean syntax. The internal _worker command is reserved for the HTTP supervisor.

Query flags

FlagApplies toMeaning
--city DIRData commandsPrepared City; overrides VIGO_CITY
--routing-store FILEData commandsWith --city naming a Studio project's .vigo folder, the timetable store in its routing/ folder to open (such as current.sqlite)
--request FILERoute, Matrix, Reach, Compare, NativeJSON file; - reads stdin
--output FILEOne-shot JSON commandsSave result; - means stdout
--prettyOne-shot JSON commandsIndent JSON
--stream-output public|detailedStreamPublic results by default; detailed internal wrapper envelope when explicitly selected
--service-date YYYY-MM-DDRoute, Matrix, Reach, Native, StreamSet or override service date
--time HH:MM[:SS]Route, Matrix, Reach, StreamSet clock; replaces JSON timeMinutes
--mode transit|walk|driveRoute, Matrix, Reach, StreamReach supports all three modes
--from lon,lat or --from stop:IDRoute, ReachOrigin
--to lon,lat or --to stop:IDRoute, ReachDestination; an arrive-by Reach takes a destination
--max-walk KMRoute, Matrix, Reach, StreamWalking endpoint budget
--max-transfers NRoute, Matrix, Reach, StreamTransit transfer cap
--max-street KMRoute, MatrixIndependent street-route distance cap
--horizon MINUTESRoute, MatrixSearch horizon
--arrive-byRoute, Matrix, ReachArrive-by time direction; false restores depart-at
--alternatives NRouteAdditional transit journeys, 0–9
--alternative-ranking pareto|rankedRouteHow alternatives are chosen
--cutoffs 15,30,45ReachTravel-time cutoffs
--raster-size NReachSquare grid width and height
--radius KMReachReporting extent radius
--street-edgesReachInclude directed street evidence
--scenario IDData commands on a collectionSelect a scenario; omission uses defaultScenario
--wheelchairRoute, Matrix, ReachRequire the City's strict wheelchair profile
--wheelchair-streetsbuildinferred (default) or verified wheelchair street evidence
--format text|jsonOne-shot JSON commandsTerminal text or JSON; pipes and files use JSON
--diagnostics LEVELQuery commandsnone, summary, profile, or trace
--include-geometry, --include-limitationsQuery commandsRoute geometry is on by default; Matrix geometry and limitations are opt-in

Server flags are listed in the HTTP API reference. Other controls, including transfer buffers, realtime, scenarios, via points, and journey geometry, belong in JSON. CLI query flags override fields from the request file. Stream flags override every line, so omit a stream-level service date when sending different dates.

Files and standard input

Input files/stdin accept one JSON object and an optional UTF-8 BOM, up to 8 MiB. A request read from stdin completes when stdin closes. JSON goes to stdout; logs/errors go to stderr. With a file output, the result is saved instead of printed. Writes are staged and renamed atomically, preserving an existing file's permissions. The output directory must already exist. No CSV batch interface is provided; use Matrix or Stream.

Engine and HTTP API

Compiler command line

3 min readSource

On this page

CommandsSend a requestKeep the compiler residentRead a response

The compiler, vigo-build, builds Cities and runs Route, Matrix, Reach, Stream, and Compare through VIGO's shared native routing kernel. The engine has its own command set; see the engine CLI reference.

Commands

CommandInputOutput
buildGTFS, OSM, output directoryA complete prepared City
build-scenariosA scenario source manifestA prepared scenario collection
capabilitiesNoneVersions and supported query combinations
inspectCity directoryIdentity, sources, counts, and limitations
routeCity and JSON requestA public journey Result, or a CSV batch
matrixCity and JSON requestAn origin-by-destination travel-time Result
reachCity and JSON requestReachable areas and optional analytical output
streamCity and NDJSON on stdinOne Result per request from a resident process
compareTwo saved ResultsChanges without rerunning routing

Run vigo-build help route or vigo-build route -h for options, and vigo-build --version for the version. Unknown options, extra positional arguments, and repeated single-value options are rejected; --gtfs, --gtfs-scope, and --prepare-date may repeat.

Send a request

Requests carry serviceDate and time in JSON, and flags override request fields exactly as in the engine:

Shell
vigo-build route --city ./boston --request route.json --output route-result.json
cat route.json | vigo-build route --city ./boston --request - --time 08:30 > route-result.json
FlagMeaning
--service-date, --timeOverride the request's date and clock (00:00–29:59)
--time-preference depart|arriveTime direction; JSON also accepts depart_at and arrive_by
--mode transit|walk|driveTravel mode
--max-walk, --max-transfers, --horizonWalking budget (km), transfer cap, timetable horizon (minutes)
--departure-window MINCentered depart-at profile of ±0–30 minutes; Route only
--alternatives N, --alternative-rankingAdditional transit journeys; Route only
--data-mode scheduled|realtimeRoute data mode; realtime needs a supplied snapshot
--cutoffs, --raster-size, --extent-radius, --walk-speed, --street-edgesReach options
--diagnostics, --format, --include-geometry, --include-limitationsOutput detail

Request files and stdin share a 16 MiB limit, and --request - reads until the producer closes stdin. Progress and errors go to stderr; JSON goes to stdout. Saved output is staged and renamed after a complete write, so a failed run can leave an earlier output file in place: check the exit code. CSV Route batches use --input with an output file, support transit only, and cannot be combined with --request.

Keep the compiler resident

stream reads one request per line, each with an explicit kind, and keeps prepared network state between lines. Each line may choose its own serviceDate; a --service-date flag only sets the default.

NDJSON
{"id":"outbound","kind":"route","origin":{"stopId":"A"},"destination":{"stopId":"B"},"serviceDate":"2026-10-05","time":"08:00"}
{"id":"times","kind":"matrix","origins":[{"stopId":"A"}],"destinations":[{"stopId":"B"}],"serviceDate":"2026-10-05","time":"08:00"}
Shell
vigo-build stream --city ./city < queries.ndjson > results.ndjson

Responses echo id and add sequence. A per-line error does not end the stream. First-use preparation, later queries, and serialization are different timing boundaries.

Read a response

Public Results identify schema, status, and query metadata: Route uses journey, Matrix durationsSeconds, and Reach surface.valuesSeconds or map-only areas, all in seconds. diagnostics: "trace" adds internal evidence under trace; applications should use the public result reference. An invalid one-shot request exits nonzero, and stream errors use schema: "vigo.error.v1" with error.code and error.message.

VIGO Python runs the same resident protocol with its own Result properties. Studio's internal application API is not a public integration boundary.

Points, clocks, units, and common fields

4 min readSource

On this page

Coordinates and stop IDsCommon query fieldsService time and walking policy

Queries accept map coordinates or stop IDs. Transit queries also need a service date and a clock time.

Coordinates and stop IDs

Use [longitude, latitude] in WGS84 decimal degrees. Longitude must be −180…180, latitude −90…90. Kilometers are used for high-level walking/street limits; output geometry distances are meters; high-level times are minutes. Native operations use seconds/meters unless a field explicitly names another unit.

JSON
{"coordinate": [-77.05, 38.9]}
JSON
{"stopId": "A"}

A point may also be a bare coordinate array. Point objects accept id, name, label, source, and scenario metadata editStatus, baselineStopId, baselineStopIndex. These labels do not change routing. A valid stopId takes precedence over a coordinate, except source: "map", which deliberately uses the coordinate. Selected stations/platforms include their prepared station members. This selection does not certify a physical path between every platform.

Exact identifiers are case-sensitive. Multi-feed IDs may contain a feed scope and the JSON separator \u001f. Obtain active IDs with timetable.identifiers; do not assume a local ID is unique in a combined City.

Common query fields

FieldDefault / requirementAccepted values and meaning
serviceDateRequired for transit/timetable operationsExact YYYY-MM-DD; calendar plus date exceptions select service
serviceDayDerivedOptional weekday, saturday, or sunday; must agree with the date
timeRequired unless timeMinutes is suppliedHH:MM[:SS], hours 0–71; numeric minutes are also accepted
timeMinutesAlternative clockNumber 0–4319; never combine with time
timePreferencedepart_atdepart_at or arrive_by; aliases depart and arrive accepted
modetransittransit, walk, drive
maxWalkKm1.2Number 0–100; per transit access/egress endpoint, Reach terminal-walk budget, or Drive walk between a point and its road
maxTransfersNo explicit capInteger 0–31; zero means at most one boarding
horizonMinutes480Number 1–2880; Route/Matrix only
maxStreetKm50Number 0.05–1000; Walk/Drive Route/Matrix limit. Zero and values below 0.05 are rejected, never rounded up or treated as unlimited.
allowStreetTransferstrueKeep or filter walking transfers between separate stops/stations
minimumTransferBufferMinutes0Integer 0–60; extra time per subsequent transit transfer
requireTransitRidefalseTransit Route/Matrix boarding policy
allowLongWalktrueTransit only: when false, cap direct walking alternatives by maxWalkKm instead of maxStreetKm. Explicit Walk mode always uses maxStreetKm
walkSpeedKphCity's walking policy, normally 4.8Number 1–8; walking legs, including a drive's walk to and from its road
disableCachefalseDisable street endpoint caches; not a complete cold-run switch
requireCompleteServiceCoveragefalseReject missing active source scopes in a multi-feed service slice
sourceScopesAll sourcesArray of source scope names; route only on the services of those sources in a multi-feed City
departNowfalseTransit Route only: leave at the current minute in the agency's timezone (rounded up), on its service date; replaces serviceDate and time
routingDataModeInferred from supplied observation inputscheduled or realtime; dataMode is an alias; do not supply both
idOptionalCaller correlation value; echoed by Stream and HTTP

Service time and walking policy

Transit times are service-day clocks, including after-midnight GTFS hours. Calendar queries include services on adjacent dates when their trips overlap the search interval. GTFS clocks use local noon minus twelve elapsed hours, including daylight-saving changes. journey.clockDate anchors every journey and leg clock; a transit leg's serviceDate identifies its actual operating date, and hours can exceed 23. Street-only queries still require a clock but can omit serviceDate.

The depart-at timetable search ends at departure plus horizon; arrive-by searches back to the later of midnight and arrival minus horizon. A transit egress walk may extend beyond the depart-at scan horizon. Direct walking is bounded by physical walking duration as well as its distance cap. Drive routing uses its street-distance limit and supplied static metric; horizonMinutes does not add a drive travel-time cutoff.

City access padding/overhead apply to boarding access, not physical direct-walk duration. The transfer buffer applies once after walking and source-defined transfer minima; it does not delay first boarding, final egress, or staying aboard. allowStreetTransfers: false retains endpoint access and egress. Neither control establishes station accessibility or fare-transfer eligibility.

arrivalBufferMinutes is an optional integer 0–60 (default 0) for arrive-by Transit Route and Matrix. A positive value reserves time before the final deadline while retaining the original earliest departure. The deadline must be at least the reserve, and horizonMinutes must exceed it by at least one minute. Positive reserves reject via points, depart-at, Walk, Drive, Reach, and native operations. diagnostics.timeReserves records both deadlines and calibratedProbability: false. Route and journey clocks retain their actual modeled times; Matrix scalar durations include the reserve. Combine with minimumTransferBufferMinutes for time at intermediate changes. See Travel-time uncertainty for the Boston example and calibration requirements; a margin is not a probability guarantee.
