Diagnostics and native output

2 min readSource

On this page

Where diagnostics liveTiming and countersNative result envelope and indices

Diagnostics explain the computation that ran. They are useful for troubleshooting and profiling, but the high-level result fields remain the values to show to clients.

Where diagnostics live

ResultDiagnostic location
Transit Routediagnostics.originAccess, destinationAccess, search, native, and realtime
Direct Walk/Drive Routediagnostics is the corresponding native street/drive result
Transit Matrixdiagnostics is the native timetable matrix result
Walk/Drive Matrixdiagnostics is the native street/drive matrix result
Reachdiagnostics.transit and diagnostics.surface; transit is null in walk-only mode
Via RoutePer-segment diagnostics under segments; no aggregate top-level search diagnostic

Transit Route search diagnostics report startSeconds, endSeconds, transfer policy, and horizonScope: "timetable_scan". Endpoint access diagnostics explain selected-stop or coordinate candidate construction. diagnostics.realtime describes an applied supplied snapshot when present; a dataMode label is not an independent prediction-accuracy guarantee.

When a direct walk wins inside a transit request, the top-level route or matrix cell reflects walking while the native diagnostics still describe the transit search. Do not overwrite the returned high-level value with a diagnostic clock or duration.

Timing and counters

queryNs / 1_000_000 converts a native query time to milliseconds. It measures a kernel scope inside dispatch; it is not network latency. Native searches, preparation, geometry materialization, and JSON construction can have different boundaries. Do not sum nested timings or subtract them to infer an isolated cost without checking their scope.

Timetable counters such as scannedDepartures, expandedTripRuns, and relaxedStops count algorithm work, not necessarily distinct trips or stops. Matrix forwardSearches and reverseSearches show execution orientation without changing row/column order. Reach reachedPixels counts finite cells on the requested grid; reachedEdgeCount and reachedEdgeLengthM count directed street edges, so two directions can represent the same physical road. They are not a geographic area measurement or a count of unique road centerlines.

Native result envelope and indices

Native responses contain operation and a typed object under result, plus outer dispatch metadata. The native field reference lists every operation's input and output type. Native result fields are present even when their optional values are null; high-level variant fields can instead be absent.

Timetable operations use indices from timetable.identifiers for the same active service date and policy. stopIds[index] resolves a stop index; tripIds[index] and routeIds[index] resolve a trip and its route. routeIds is parallel to trips, not a deduplicated route catalog. accessMemberStopIds belongs to prepared endpoint-access members, a separate domain. Do not reuse saved numeric indices across changed preparations or timetable activations.

Native timetable.matrix returns a flat origin-major times array of service-day clock seconds. For one A → B pair, the fixture route's departure gives [30600], an 08:30 arrival. Arrive-by gives latest departure clocks instead. journeys is null when not requested; an unreachable numeric slot serializes as null. Street and drive native matrices use flat distances in meters and, for drive, durations in seconds. Read the operation-specific type before interpreting an array named times, values, or distancesM.

PreviousComparison outputNextStreaming
Engine and HTTP API

Resident NDJSON streaming

2 min readSource

Keep a City loaded while sending a sequence of JSON queries through standard input. Streaming returns one result for each request, in order.

One-shot commands open a City for each invocation. stream keeps a City resident and reads one object per line. Every line requires kind; an optional id is echoed even for query errors. Output is one compact JSON object per line, in input order, carrying the request id and a sequence number like the compiler's stream. Blank lines are ignored, and there is no startup handshake.

Transit can reuse a prepared service snapshot only when its source database, access policy, active services, transfer projection, dictionaries, and array layout validate. Missing or invalid optional timetable snapshots fall back to source preparation without writing City files. Realtime and disabled street transfers use source preparation. For repeated calls, keep stream or serve resident; measure fresh-process startup separately from warm query time. The runtime retains immutable shape/alignment data in a bounded cache (1,024 shapes and 64 MiB by default; configurable through VIGO_SHAPE_GEOMETRY_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES and VIGO_SHAPE_GEOMETRY_CACHE_MAX_BYTES) and shares same-request endpoint evidence even when answer caches are disabled. The shape limit is an upper bound, not reserved memory; it trades a larger possible resident footprint for less repeated geometry preparation.

Full Matrix journeys also share immutable ride and walking evidence within the request, bounded to 4,096 entries and 16 MiB of estimated storage. The key retains the selected endpoint candidates, stop/sequence identities and walking cost; each occurrence keeps its own service clocks. Geometry is unchanged. This storage is discarded after the matrix, including when the query fails. Disabling request caches does not disable this sharing inside one batch.

NDJSON
{"kind":"route","id":"trip-1","origin":{"stopId":"A"},"destination":{"stopId":"B"},"serviceDate":"2026-07-15","time":"07:55","maxWalkKm":0.2}
{"kind":"reach","id":"area-1","origin":{"stopId":"A"},"serviceDate":"2026-07-15","time":"07:55","cutoffsMinutes":[30],"rasterSize":48,"extentRadiusKm":2}
Shell
./vigo stream --city ./city < requests.ndjson > results.ndjson

Route, Matrix, Reach/isochrone, Compare, Native, Info, and Capabilities use the same dispatcher. The process retains the latest active timetable; a different service date is allowed and replaces that timetable. This differs from the older Node stream's fixed-date process. Malformed JSON/invalid queries produce per-line errors and the next line can run. A line exceeding 8 MiB terminates the stream. Stream has no query deadline or supervised restart; use HTTP or your own process supervisor for those guarantees. Close stdin to end it.

EndpointsServer limitsCancel a requestStatus codesSend a request

Start the HTTP service with vigo serve and send query JSON to the endpoints below. The command line and HTTP API use the same request fields.

Endpoints

Method/pathResponseAuthentication

POST /v1/nativeTyped native operationBearer when configured; otherwise local Host/Origin
DELETE /v1/requests/{id}Cancel a named requestBearer when configured; otherwise local Host/Origin

The path selects the command; a body kind is overwritten accordingly. Send JSON with Content-Type: application/json. Content-Length and bounded chunked HTTP/1.1 bodies are supported. Duplicate/conflicting length headers are rejected. Connections close after a response; there is no keep-alive, WebSocket, HTTP/2, gzip, streaming response, or browser CORS policy in the service. Other methods/paths return 404 after authentication. A same-origin application or reverse proxy can provide a browser integration policy. Every response carries a restrictive Content-Security-Policy; it allows the embedded guide's API console to call this service's own endpoints (connect-src 'self') and nothing else.

Server limits

The executable runs an HTTP front end and a supervised child worker. The worker keeps one City loaded and processes one query at a time; individual queries can use native parallel kernels. Slow request bodies are read outside that worker. Queue deadlines include waiting and writing to the child. A timed-out or failed worker is stopped and replaced. The service holds no per-client session.

Server optionDefaultAllowed range
--host127.0.0.1Literal IPv4/IPv6 address; not a hostname
--portPORT, otherwise 80800–65535; zero selects an ephemeral port
--max-body-bytes83886081024–8388608
--request-timeout-ms1000050–60000; absolute request read deadline
--query-timeout-ms300001–600000; queued/dispatched computation
--max-connections322–256
--max-queue80–128 waiting jobs
--realtime-pollNoneGTFS-RT polling settings file; see Automatic GTFS-RT polling

Queued HTTP requests retain encoded JSON; only the worker expands nested query fields. Across connections, uploads and queued requests share a 64 MiB encoded-byte admission budget (including normalization headroom). Chunked uploads reserve their configured maximum before reading. Pending response buffers share a 128 MiB budget until socket writes finish. Capacity exhaustion returns 503, including before 100 Continue for rejected uploads. These bounds cover transport buffers, not total process RSS or the City working set; response reading can additionally hold one worker result of up to 64 MiB. Closing, canceling, or expiring a request releases its reservation when its retained work is discarded.

Waiting routes and matrices of at most 1,024 cells receive up to 32 turns or 250 ms of worker time before the oldest waiting analytical request. FIFO order is preserved within each group, and one admission limit covers both groups. This prevents a submitted batch of Reach jobs from monopolizing the waiting queue. The worker completes its current query before switching; a long running query still contributes to latency.

Headers are limited to 16 KiB and 64 header entries. Worker output is limited to 64 MiB per result. Response writing has a 10-second deadline; startup allows up to 60 seconds for a City worker. Oversized responses or worker exits can appear as 504, so split high-detail matrices/rasters rather than retrying the same oversized query indefinitely.

Cancel a request

A named HTTP request (id containing up to 128 letters, digits, hyphens, underscores or periods) can be canceled through DELETE /v1/requests/{id}. The cancellation returns 202; the original request returns 499. Running work is terminated and its worker replaced; queued work is skipped. Retrying an ID while it is active returns 409.

Status codes

HTTP statusMeaning
200Computed result, including blocked Route; or successful metadata/documentation
400Invalid query, JSON, or HTTP framing
401Missing/incorrect bearer token
403Without a token: request not addressed to a loopback name, or a browser Origin other than the service's own
404Unsupported path or method
408Request read deadline
409A request with the same id is still active
413Request body over limit
417Unsupported Expect header
431Header byte limit
499The request was canceled through DELETE /v1/requests/{id}
503Connection/queue/buffer capacity or worker unavailable; readiness also uses this
504Query deadline, worker failure, or response-channel failure

The service logs its listening address to stderr. Health routes avoid the computation queue but still share the connection limit. A failed accept or connection setup, such as descriptor exhaustion, drops that connection and the service keeps listening; accept failures pause briefly before the next attempt. If a replacement City worker fails to start, the first failure of each streak is logged with its reason, /readyz returns 503 and queries return 503 while restarts back off exponentially from 250 ms to at most 10 seconds. Use bounded retries with backoff for 503; for 504 first reduce the workload or inspect worker logs. Do not treat a transport error as an unreachable trip.

Engine and HTTP API
Client integration
1 min readSource
Send query JSON from your application through HTTP or the command line. An HTTP client needs no VIGO language package.


Use the standalone response fields described in Results and errors. The public Node and Rust result schemas are shared; old internal envelopes are retained only in trace. For reproducible jobs, keep the build identity, capabilities, City revision, complete request, observation timestamps, and output.


A Python standard-library HTTP client needs no VIGO Python package:


Python
import json
import os
import urllib.error
import urllib.request

query = {
    "origin": {"stopId": "A"},
    "destination": {"stopId": "B"},
    "serviceDate": "2026-07-15",
    "time": "07:55",
    "maxWalkKm": 0.2,
}
headers = {"Content-Type": "application/json"}
if os.environ.get("VIGO_API_TOKEN"):
    headers["Authorization"] = "Bearer " + os.environ["VIGO_API_TOKEN"]
request = urllib.request.Request(
    "http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/route",
    data=json.dumps(query).encode(), headers=headers,
)
try:
    with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=45) as response:
        result = json.load(response)
except urllib.error.HTTPError as error:
    raise RuntimeError(error.read().decode()) from error
if result.get("status") == "not_found":
    print("No journey:", result.get("reason"))
else:
    print(result["journey"]["arrivalTime"], result["journey"]["legs"])


A JavaScript client can use fetch with an AbortSignal timeout. Read the HTTP status before interpreting JSON; its successful body can still be a blocked result. Keep bearer tokens in server-side integrations or an appropriate authenticated same-origin service. Do not embed a shared deployment token into publicly served application code.

Native operation reference
2 min readSource
Call the routing kernels directly when you need packed arrays or controls exposed by a native operation.


Use vigo native --city ./city --request kernel-query.json or POST /v1/native. Supply operation, input, and a service date for timetable operations. Native indices must belong to the loaded City and active service date. The HTTP API never accepts a filesystem path inside a query.


JSON
{
  "operation": "timetable.identifiers",
  "serviceDate": "2026-07-15"
}


timetable.identifiers returns stopIds, tripIds, routeIds (one per active trip), and accessMemberStopIds. An index is its position in the corresponding array. Resolve each active timetable's IDs before building numeric requests. Cumulative offset arrays start at zero, end at the associated packed-array length, and have one more entry than their group count. Parallel arrays must have equal compatible lengths; indices and times are validated by the kernels.


An ordinary street path uses coordinates and needs no numeric timetable IDs:


JSON
{
  "operation": "street.path",
  "input": {
    "originLon": -77.05,
    "originLat": 38.9,
    "destinationLon": -77.03,
    "destinationLat": 38.91,
    "maximumDistanceM": 5000,
    "maximumPoints": 512
  }
}


Native timetable departure, horizon, earliest, and deadline are absolute service-day seconds. High-level horizonMinutes is a duration; native horizon is an end clock. maximumBoardings counts vehicle boardings, so it equals a high-level transfer cap plus one. Access walk times and transfer arrays are seconds, distances are meters. Drive traffic weights use hundredths of seconds. Native output suffixes such as queryNs retain nanoseconds and must not be relabeled milliseconds.


Native Matrix returns a flat array of clock times in seconds: arrival clocks for depart-at, departure clocks for arrive-by. High-level Matrix returns a two-dimensional array of travel durations in minutes. Both use origin row order and destination column order. Unreachable native times are serialized as null.


timetable.pareto exposes native arrival/boarding/walking trade-offs; it is distinct from sampled departure windows. Native overlays operate on packed caller-supplied arrays. realtime.compile compiles explicit effective call times; it does not fetch/decode a provider feed. The native field reference lists every public operation and nested input/result type from the Rust definitions. Optional request fields may be omitted or set to null. Native result objects include every declared field; unavailable optional values are null. The runtime also enforces semantic limits and compatible array domains.


The complete generated dictionary is in Native Rust field reference. It is also part of the offline guide and the engine archive.

Operate
Deploy the routing engine
3 min readSource
On this page
Build and check the imageStart the serviceResource controlsRun without DockerOperate and upgrade
Run the engine executable as the HTTP service. It opens a prepared City or scenario collection without Node, Python, Studio, or an internet connection. Prepare data separately with the compiler, then mount the complete output directory read-only.


Build and check the image


From the repository root with Docker installed:


Shell
docker build -f deploy/Dockerfile -t vigo:1.0.0-rc.2 .


The image contains the engine with this guide embedded, license notices, and a Debian glibc runtime, and runs as UID/GID 65532. Its compiler matches rust-toolchain.toml; City data, JavaScript dependencies, desktop bundles, and build caches are excluded from the build context. Check the image before using it:


Shell
npm ci
npm run build:cli-runtime
npm run check:deployment -- --image vigo:1.0.0-rc.2


The check builds public synthetic inputs and exercises the real Compose service: a read-only City, authentication, Route, Matrix, Reach, scenario switching, readiness, restart, and resource limits, and it confirms that queries never change City files. CI runs it on Linux x64 and ARM64. Measure your own City and request mix before choosing production limits; the small fixture is not a metropolitan memory or latency result.


Start the service


Make the City directory and its files readable by UID 65532, and keep every referenced directory inside the mounted City or collection.


Shell
export VIGO_IMAGE=vigo:1.0.0-rc.2
export VIGO_CITY=/absolute/path/to/prepared-city
# Set VIGO_API_TOKEN through your shell or deployment secret store (16+ characters).
docker compose -f deploy/compose.yml up -d --wait


The service binds to 127.0.0.1:8080 on the host; put an HTTPS reverse proxy in front of it for remote clients. Query endpoints require Authorization: Bearer ..., while readiness and this guide are public.


Shell
curl --fail-with-body http://127.0.0.1:8080/readyz
curl --fail-with-body http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/route \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VIGO_API_TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @route.json
docker compose -f deploy/compose.yml logs --tail 50


GET /v1/info reports network, query-workspace, cache, and scenario-residency accounting. For scheduled comparisons, pass scenarioId with each query; a scenario collection stores shared regional data once and keeps a bounded number of scenarios resident. The HTTP API lists every endpoint and status code.


Resource controls


Compose defaults to 2 CPUs, 2 GiB of memory, two native threads, two resident scenarios, and one native query worker with a bounded queue. It uses a read-only root filesystem and City mount, drops Linux capabilities, and caps logs at two 5 MB files.


Environment settingDefaultMeaning
VIGO_LOCAL_PORT8080Loopback port on the host
VIGO_CPUS / VIGO_MEMORY2 / 2gContainer CPU and memory limits
VIGO_THREADS2Native parallel threads
VIGO_MAX_RESIDENT_SCENARIOS2Maximum resident scenario views
VIGO_RESIDENT_HEAP_BYTESmin(1 GiB, memory / 3)Collection retained-heap budget; one selected City may exceed it, reported by /v1/info; not an RSS limit
VIGO_ENDPOINT_CACHE_MAX_BYTES8388608Shared endpoint-cache budget
VIGO_SHAPE_GEOMETRY_CACHE_MAX_BYTES8388608Shared geometry-cache budget
VIGO_MAX_QUEUE8Waiting queries
VIGO_MAX_CONNECTIONS16Active HTTP connections
VIGO_MAX_BODY_BYTES8388608Maximum request body
VIGO_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS10000Request and response I/O timeout
VIGO_QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS30000Queue and execution deadline


Before raising these limits, read Resource limits and constrained serving: extra processes are not a free speedup, and swap is never counted as RAM.


The worker reuses its network and workspaces, prioritizes short queries, and gives queued analytical work a bounded turn. A deadline or cancellation terminates running work and reloads the worker, and readiness is unavailable during recovery. A full queue returns an error instead of accepting unbounded work. Responses are limited to 64 MiB; split large matrices or omit geometry when appropriate.


GET /healthz checks the HTTP process and GET /readyz checks worker availability. The container runs vigo health against /readyz; the probe loads no City and needs no shell, curl, or Node. The restart policy restarts exited containers, not merely unhealthy ones.


Run without Docker


The engine archive runs directly: vigo serve --city ./city --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080, checked with vigo health --port 8080. Authentication and hosting covers tokens, reverse proxies, and a systemd unit.


Operate and upgrade


Prepare a new City in a separate directory, verify saved requests against the candidate, and switch the image and City together. Never replace files that a running service has mapped, and keep the previous accepted image and City for rollback; see Upgrade and rollback. Service benchmarking records cold start, first-query and sustained latency, memory, and disk costs. Stop the service with docker compose -f deploy/compose.yml down; the City stays on the host.

Authentication and generic deployment
3 min readSource
On this page
Environment and authenticationContainerProcess manager
Start locally with a prepared City directory. For remote access, configure an API token and put the service behind an HTTPS proxy.


Environment and authentication


The environment variables for the Rust runtime are:


VariablePurpose
VIGO_CITYDefault prepared City path; overridden by --city
PORTDefault HTTP port; overridden by --port
VIGO_API_TOKENBearer token; nonempty values protect data endpoints, including loopback
RAYON_NUM_THREADSOptional native parallel thread count
VIGO_MAX_RESIDENT_SCENARIOSMaximum resident scenario views
VIGO_RESIDENT_HEAP_BYTESCollection retained-heap budget; default min(1 GiB, detected memory / 3), positive integer
VIGO_TIMETABLE_CACHE_BYTESInactive scheduled-timetable budget per City or collection; default 134217728 bytes, 0 disables retention
VIGO_ENDPOINT_CACHE_MAX_BYTESShared endpoint-cache budget
VIGO_SHAPE_GEOMETRY_CACHE_MAX_BYTESShared geometry-cache budget


A non-loopback bind requires a token at least 16 characters long. Set it through your deployment secret mechanism and send Authorization: Bearer .... Without a token, a loopback service accepts data requests only when Host is 127.0.0.1, localhost or [::1] (with an optional port) and any Origin header is that same http:// origin; other requests return 403 forbidden. This blocks DNS-rebinding and cross-site browser requests, as in Studio. Clients that send a different Host, such as a local reverse proxy, should set VIGO_API_TOKEN. The static manual/specification and health endpoints remain public; they contain no query or City data. The token is not a CLI argument and the service does not persist tokens or query bodies.


Shell
export VIGO_CITY=/srv/vigo/city
# Set VIGO_API_TOKEN through your shell or platform secret store.
./vigo serve --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080 \
  --query-timeout-ms 30000 --max-queue 8 --max-connections 32

curl --fail-with-body http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/route \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VIGO_API_TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @route.json


Terminate HTTPS at a reverse proxy or hosting platform. Give its upstream timeout room for the chosen query deadline plus request/response transfer. Mount City data read-only and set process/container memory and CPU limits according to measured workloads. Scale with multiple service processes/containers, each with its own resident collection and bounded query queue. There is no globally shared queue, distributed cache, tenant management, or server-side request persistence.


Container


Build the native service image from the repository root:


Shell
docker build -f deploy/Dockerfile -t vigo:1.0.0-rc.2 .
export VIGO_IMAGE=vigo:1.0.0-rc.2
export VIGO_CITY=/absolute/path/to/prepared-city
# Set VIGO_API_TOKEN through your deployment secret store.
docker compose -f deploy/compose.yml up -d --wait


The image runs as UID/GID 65532 on Debian glibc, with the native executable and its embedded documentation. Compose mounts the City read-only and defaults to 2 CPUs, 2 GiB, a bounded query queue, bounded caches, and limited log storage. The built-in vigo health command checks worker readiness without loading a City or requiring an external runtime. Give UID 65532 read and traversal access to the City.


See Deploy the routing engine for the complete configuration and container acceptance check.


Process manager


For a generic Linux host, install the matching binary and configure an unprivileged service account, readable City directory, and protected environment file. A systemd unit can use:


INI
[Unit]
Description=VIGO Rust routing service
After=network.target

[Service]
User=vigo
Group=vigo
EnvironmentFile=/etc/vigo/runtime.env
ExecStart=/opt/vigo/vigo serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080
Restart=on-failure
NoNewPrivileges=true
ProtectSystem=strict
ProtectHome=true
PrivateTmp=true
KillMode=control-group

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target


Set VIGO_CITY and, when desired, VIGO_API_TOKEN in the environment file. Stop the service through the process manager so its worker is also cleaned up. Allow active requests to finish before stopping; queued requests may be interrupted during shutdown.

Resource limits and constrained serving
3 min readSource
On this page
Capacity-aware defaultsScenario and date switchingSwap is an explicit deployment choiceValidation boundaries
Python batch concurrency and Engine query concurrency have different costs. City.iter_run(queries, workers=2) overlaps complete queries using separate resident processes. Each owns its prepared City. The native HTTP service uses one supervised query worker with bounded admission, deadlines, cancellation and recovery; its routing kernel can parallelize supported work internally. On a 2 CPU / 2 GiB deployment, keep one resident query process and two native threads. Additional processes are not a free speedup.


The native endpoint-access pool also follows available CPU parallelism (including Linux quota/affinity) and a positive RAYON_NUM_THREADS cap, up to four threads. With one available thread it runs sequentially without creating a pool. This shares one City and preserves exact endpoint searches.


Capacity-aware defaults


At startup, native cache defaults use the smallest reported Linux physical-memory, cgroup v2 memory.max/memory.high, or cgroup v1 memory limit. Visible ancestor limits are included. Unlimited values are ignored. Non-Linux and unknown-capacity installations retain the existing bounded cache defaults. Explicit cache settings remain operator overrides.


Native allocationDefault upper boundFraction of detected capacity
Endpoint cache, per role64 MiB1/64
Shape geometry cache64 MiB1/64
Inactive timetables128 MiB1/32
HTTP pending request bytes64 MiB1/32
HTTP retained response bytes128 MiB1/16


HTTP budgets preserve room for one maximum-sized request and one worker response line. Caches are optional retained work: reducing them does not truncate journeys or change routing results. Collections partition the applicable caches across resident scenarios. The active City and query scratch are outside these cache budgets; a small cache does not prove a large network will fit.


vigo info and /v1/info report resourcePolicy.memoryCapacityBytes and swapCountsAsRam. Capacity is a startup sizing input, not current free memory or a hard process RSS guarantee. Linux controllers at nonstandard mount locations require explicit operator limits. Restart after changing controller limits.


Python caps its existing one-to-four worker budget using affinity, CPU quota and the same visible Linux memory-controller hierarchy. Unknown memory capacity selects one worker. On all platforms, workers=1 remains the public batch default.


Scenario and date switching


For collections, inspect /v1/info residency counters before attributing latency to route search. Increasing cityOpens and evictions on repeated scenario sweeps indicates that retained Cities exceed VIGO_RESIDENT_HEAP_BYTES, even when the scenario-count limit permits them. Tune the heap budget only with measured container peaks and concurrent requests; leave room for query scratch, mapped pages and other services. The default remains conservative. When the retained heap exceeds this budget, the collection discards optional timetable/source cache entries before evicting a resident City; active timetables and street preparation are preserved while reclaimable cache entries remain.


Changing service dates can rebuild a timetable when the inactive-timetable cache is too small. Large scheduled slices can reuse losslessly compressed source columns within that same byte budget. Their keys include the active services, service dates/offsets and query horizon; realtime and linked-trip expansion run after restoration. Compression uses reversible numeric deltas and streaming buffers, without a second uncompressed schedule. Full kernels remain reusable when several fit; compact sources allow more dates to fit on constrained hosts. First reads still require SQLite preparation, and cache eviction remains possible. Immutable linked-trip and block adjacency is retained with its City and included in the heap ledger; active service, realtime cancellations and continuity are still checked for each timetable. Native trace timing separates linkedCandidatesMs and linkedTripsMs within sourceAndRealtimeMs, and reports linkedCandidatesReused. These are preparation measurements, not end-to-end HTTP latency.


Swap is an explicit deployment choice


The Compose service disables swap by default by setting total RAM-plus-swap equal to RAM. To permit up to 4 GiB of swap alongside 2 GiB RAM, use VIGO_MEMORY=2g VIGO_MEMORY_SWAP=6g. The Linux host must already provide sufficient swap; Compose does not create it. A swap-free comparison uses VIGO_MEMORY_SWAP=2g.


Swap is never added to the resident capacity used to size workers or caches. It can preserve cold anonymous pages under pressure, but may substantially increase latency. File-backed mappings can be reclaimed independently. Record RSS, cgroup current/peak memory, swap usage, memory events, pressure and request latency separately; container memory includes page cache and is not RSS. See the Linux memory-controller specification for the accounting rules.


Validation boundaries


The deployment check exercises the shipped image and Compose file at 2 GiB and a 256 MiB synthetic collection, including full geometry, scenario eviction, restart parity and read-only City integrity. The small fixture validates controls and recovery; it does not establish that a regional City fits in 256 MiB. Regional endurance and swap tests need retained workload-specific evidence, including errors and OOM counters, before making a deployment claim.

Runtime memory and caching
6 min readSource
On this page
Shared data across scenariosTimetable preparation and retentionQuery workspaces and residencyMemory ledgerCaches and responses
A resident stream or serve process keeps its City, timetable, and street indexes ready between requests. This chapter describes what it shares, what it retains, and how to account for memory.


Shared data across scenarios


Resident Cities share immutable street arrays and CCH indexes by canonical path. Timetable source columns share equal immutable blocks across resident scenarios. A hash selects candidates, and every reuse checks all values; changes occupy independent blocks without an overlay chain. The collection holds weak references to shared blocks, so evicting their last timetable view releases the data. Stop and trip identities, search indexes, endpoint caches and realtime state remain scenario-specific. The collection still stores separate transit databases and prepared access profiles.


Timetable preparation and retention


Scheduled timetables retain a service-clock prefix through at least 06:00 the next day. Longer requests extend that prefix in six-hour blocks; narrower requests reuse it. Future days are read only through the loaded departure bound. Realtime uses the unfiltered source so an update can move a later trip into the query window. That source read is retained (up to two service-day windows), so a new snapshot derives its view from memory instead of reading the City database again; trip, stop and transfer inputs are shared rather than rebuilt. GET /v1/info reports timetablePreparations and timetableCoverageEndSeconds for each resident scenario.


Cold startup opens the City and prepares the first requested service date. Timetable preparation reads trip-sized groups and restores the canonical date order in native arrays; it does not require a new City format or extra disk index. Keep stream or serve resident to reuse this work across requests.


Each standalone City also retains up to eight inactive scheduled timetables, with a default 128 MiB budget set by VIGO_TIMETABLE_CACHE_BYTES. Returning to a retained date and transfer policy reuses its prepared arrays and indexes. Entries use exact dates and sufficient time coverage, preserving calendar exceptions, overnight service and timezone offsets. Least recently used entries are evicted, and oversized entries are not retained. The latest two realtime views are also retained, so alternating scheduled and realtime queries do not rebuild them; a realtime view only uses space no scheduled timetable or retained source needs, because it rebuilds from its source in a fraction of a source read. Set the budget to 0 to disable date retention. This is an additional budget, separate from the active timetable, street data and preparation temporaries. A standalone City receives the full budget. In a scenario collection, retained entries keep their byte allocation and the selected scenario can borrow unused capacity from the collection budget. This avoids a fixed per-scenario share; it does not evict another resident's retained dates to make room. Separate workers each have their own budget. Shared blocks are charged in full for cache admission. memory.timetableCache reports entries, charged retainedBytes, budgetBytes, hits and evictions. Collection residency reports aggregate inactiveTimetableBudgetBytes and inactiveTimetableRetainedBytes. Retained-date activation does not trigger Linux preparation-memory trimming unless retention evicts another timetable. Matrix and Reach still reclaim their temporary allocations after completion. The owner-level memory ledger includes inactive timetables and counts shared blocks once. Calendar rules load once per City as weekday masks plus dated exceptions. Standalone Cities also share equal immutable source-column blocks across retained dates; date-specific scan indexes remain separate. The first-date layout stays contiguous until another date is retained. memory.calendarIndexBytes and memory.timetableSharedColumns expose the index and shared storage.


Query workspaces and residency


One timetable query workspace belongs to the sequential worker and is lent to the selected scenario. Boarding layers, predecessors and generation tags are rebound to its stop and run dimensions; results never cross scenarios. Reusable street-search buffers move with the active request. Exact street attachments for Reach are shared only after scenario-specific station exits are resolved, with a limit of 16,384 coordinates per street graph.


The least recently used City is evicted before opening another when maximumResidentScenarios is reached, retaining the street graph even with a one-City budget. VIGO_MAX_RESIDENT_SCENARIOS overrides this count from 1 to 16; this bounds resident scenarios. VIGO_RESIDENT_HEAP_BYTES additionally bounds collection retention using tracked heap ownership (default: the smaller of 1 GiB and one third of the detected memory capacity). Least-recently-used Cities leave before an estimated replacement allocation and after queries when measured retained heap exceeds the budget. The selected City is always retained; residentHeapOverBudget reports when that City alone exceeds the budget. This is not an RSS limit: mapped pages, allocator overhead and temporary preparation allocations require additional capacity. residency.lastQueryTiming separates scenario selection, City opening, execution and post-query retention; eviction time is a subphase of selection/retention, not an extra additive duration. Profile/trace queries separately report timetable activation and preparation inside execution. GET /v1/info reports current residency, unique timetable block bytes, column-view bytes and query-workspace bytes without opening every scenario. Timetable sourceArrayBytes measures logical column contents, including shared values; do not sum it as exclusive memory.


Memory ledger


The collection's memory ledger separates network allocations, query workspaces, caches, SQLite allocations and mapped file lengths. Its trackedHeapBytes counts shared street and timetable owners once. Each City's memory.ledger provides the component breakdown. Vector capacities are counted; hash-table and JSON-container overheads are estimates. Mapped file lengths are not resident memory. Record process-tree PSS/anonymous memory and cgroup file cache alongside the ledger; active-query temporaries, serialized responses and the application UI have separate lifetimes.


Set VIGO_MEMORY_ACCOUNTING=1 for a diagnostic run to include the last query's raw/public result-tree capacities and their overlap. This walks result objects and is disabled by default; use a separate run for latency measurements.


Node routing workers in one process share admitted immutable street snapshots and CCH files, while keeping mutable query state separate. Admission uses canonical paths and file identities. Weak references release retired networks; replacing a prepared file gives new readers a new owner. Prepared files must remain immutable while mapped. Studio GTFS/OSM import and merge run in disposable child processes. Completion reaches the serving process only after the compiler exits, so compiler allocator arenas cannot remain in the server. Preparation job records retain the compiler process count, largest process RSS peak and last process exit snapshot.


The Node driving kernel retains typed views of its immutable integer road arrays; callers must not mutate them while the kernel exists. The standalone constructor moves owned arrays. Traffic updates use separate mutable weights and leave the base graph intact. sourceArrayBytes is logical array storage, shared with JavaScript when zeroCopyArrays is true, and must not be added twice.


Caches and responses


The HTTP supervisor forwards the worker's validated JSON bytes without constructing another journey or raster object tree. The 64 MiB response limit still applies. Server-Timing's serialize entry measures supervisor serialization; forwarded results report zero there, and serialization in the query worker remains part of end-to-end HTTP time.


The endpoint and shape cache byte budgets apply to the whole collection: each resident receives a share of the configured budget. The defaults allow 64 MiB for each endpoint role and 64 MiB for shape geometry across all residents. Set VIGO_ENDPOINT_CACHE_MAX_BYTES and VIGO_SHAPE_GEOMETRY_CACHE_MAX_BYTES to change those totals. Street search and isochrone lookup pages are allocated only where a query writes. Path scratch above 32 MiB and each dynamic CCH workspace above 64 MiB are discarded before the next query; the inverse street order is retained separately. Access-profile format 6 uses bitmap ranks and offsets for nonempty buckets, and requires rebuilding earlier prepared profiles. On Linux with glibc, freed temporary pages are returned after timetable preparation, Matrix, and Reach. Measure the working set for your region and workload; timetable data and mapped street pages remain outside the result-cache budgets.

Upgrade and rollback
2 min readSource
On this page
Before changing versionsPrepared City policyValidate, switch, and recoverChecks you can run yourself
Keep a running application and its prepared City together until the replacement passes your saved requests. A new release does not by itself make an older City compatible or incompatible; the prepared-data contract decides.


Before changing versions


  1. Save the runtime version, package checksum, capabilities output, and City inspection (vigo info --city ./city, or vigo-build inspect --city ./city).
  2. Keep the original GTFS and OSM inputs, their checksums, build options, and any scenario definitions. Prepared data is not a substitute for sources.
  3. Keep representative Route, Matrix, and Reach requests and their expected Results, including your transfer, walking, and arrive-by constraints.


Prepared City policy


V1 preserves the permanent prepared-data baseline: readers open compatible Cities without rebuilding, and standard writers remain compatible with the pinned reference runtime. The prepared-data contract defines that promise and its release gate.


Cities that predate the supported prepared-data format are not converted. Rebuild them from the original sources into a different output directory:


Shell
vigo-build build --gtfs feed.zip --osm region.osm.pbf --output ./city-next
vigo info --city ./city-next
vigo route --city ./city-next --request route.json


The runtime checks timetable, transfer, street, access, and accelerator formats separately, so the outer vigo.city.v1 manifest alone is not enough, and editing a format marker cannot migrate contents. Optional query caches may be regenerated from an admitted City. Treat published City files as immutable while a service has them open.


Validate, switch, and recover


Run the saved requests against the candidate through the interface your application actually uses. Check schemas, no-journey outcomes, walking geometry, arrival and departure times, boardings, and resource use, and test a cold start as well as repeated requests. Start a second service with city-next, check readiness, and replay the requests before switching the application endpoint. Roll back by restoring the previous binary and City together, and never overwrite a live memory-mapped City.


Checks you can run yourself


From a source checkout with the documented toolchain:


Shell
npm ci
npm run build:cli-runtime
npm run build:standalone
npm run check:correctness
npm run check:public-results
npm run check:portability
npm run package:standalone
python3 test/check-standalone-package.py


These use public synthetic inputs and cover independent objective verification, difficult routing cases, public schemas, City relocation, and operation from the extracted package. They need no private benchmark files or maintainer service. Platform CI runs the broader release checks; a local pass does not establish that unrun platforms passed. Use the service benchmark to keep comparable latency and storage measurements for your workload.

Troubleshooting
6 min readSource
On this page
Check the runtime and CityBuild or open failsA request is rejectedRoute returns no journeyLive reports and routes disagreeResults or comparisons look unexpectedReport a reproducible issueConcurrent stream queriesEngine and HTTP service
Identify which stage failed: installation, City build or open, request validation, computation, or interpretation. Keep the failing command and its output before changing inputs. For a version change, follow Upgrade and rollback first.


Check the runtime and City


Shell
vigo --version
vigo capabilities --pretty
vigo info --city ./boston --pretty
vigo-build help route


capabilities describes the running binary and info identifies the City. Neither proves that a date has service or that a route is reachable. Source changes take effect only after rebuilding.


Build or open fails


SymptomCheckNext step
Node version errornode --version against the declared requirementInstall Node.js 24.18 or newer
Native build or load failureOS and CPU, the pinned Rust toolchain, and the native linkerBuild on the machine type that will run VIGO; executables are not portable, City data is
Output City already existsWhether this is a new revision or a replacementPrefer a new output directory; use --replace only for an intended replacement
Missing or corrupt street filesWhether the entire City was copiedRestore a complete City or rebuild; never copy individual databases between Cities
Expected a prepared vigo.city.v1 CityThe --city pathPoint to the compiler's complete output containing network.json
Missing or stale access or CCH artifactWhether files came from different buildsRebuild or recopy the whole City with a compatible compiler
Unexpected SQLite WALWhether the build completedComplete the build and copy a consistent, immutable City
First query slower than later onesWhether timetable or access preparation ranUse --prepare-date, and separate preparation from resident query time
City absent from Studio's libraryWhich interface created itStudio imports its own projects and cannot open compiler City directories


A request is rejected


SymptomCheck
Invalid or uncovered dateUse an exact local YYYY-MM-DD; inspect calendar.txt and calendar_dates.txt
A flag seems to ignore the JSONFlags override request fields; remove the flag or the field
Point cannot be resolvedUse an exact, case-sensitive stop ID or [longitude, latitude]; place names are not geocoded
Unknown point fieldWrite points as {"coordinate": [...]} or {"stopId": "..."}, with optional id and name; the compiler's older {"id", "point"} matrix form is not accepted by the engine
Transfer cap with transit waypointsUnsupported; omit the cap or change the experiment
Realtime or Scenario rejected by Matrix or ReachSee the support table
Matrix request too largeThe compiler allows 100,000 pairs in 16 MiB, the engine 65,536 pairs in 8 MiB
Piped request appears to wait--request - waits for one complete object and for stdin to close


Invalid requests exit with status 2 and explain the failure on stderr. If an old --output file exists, a failed run can leave it unchanged; do not mistake it for a fresh Result.


Route returns no journey


A public Route returns status: "not_found" when no journey satisfies the request. Read warnings and quality, then request diagnostics: "trace" for searchLimits and accessAvailability.


  1. Confirm the City revision, date, time, and mode. GTFS time 25:10 belongs to the previous calendar day's service date, not to a new day at 01:10.
  2. Check whether transit is required. A direct walk competes by default; requireTransitRide: true requires a boarding.
  3. Check each endpoint's walking access. A stop that is close in a straight line may lack a verified street path, and outside_selected_budget only proposes a wider check.
  4. Check the horizon, transfer cap, and timetable. For depart-at, the horizon bounds boarding and alighting, not door-to-door duration.
  5. If a changed constraint is justified, save it as a new request and keep the blocked Result as part of the analysis.


Never silently raise walking limits, substitute service dates, or turn blocked durations into zero. Route diagnostics explain the bounded failure categories.


Live reports and routes disagree


ObservationInterpretation
A vehicle is visible but its trip is unavailable to RouteVehicle Positions do not create timetable service; added-service display and routing admission are separate
Realtime times equal the scheduleUnreported trips keep scheduled times; read admitted and excluded counts and any fallback
A saved snapshot stops applying laterFreshness is checked against the captured clock; a saved observation is not live forever
An alert describes a disruption but the route is unchangedText alerts are display evidence and close nothing automatically
Playback shows a vehicle that is not reportingScheduled playback is labeled Estimated and interpolates the timetable


Keep the service date, source scope, trip identity, feed timestamp, and record timestamp together. See Network and Routes and realtime routing.


Results or comparisons look unexpected


A Matrix ok status can include unreachable null cells, and arrive-by Matrix durations include destination waiting. Matrix comparison requires identical ordered endpoints and Reach comparison identical grids; means exclude unreachable cells. For a path that appears to jump to a platform, inspect its station-path and coordinate-snap qualifications: a visible line is not evidence of an entrance connection.


Report a reproducible issue


Include the VIGO version, OS and CPU, the failing command, the request, the City inspection summary, stderr, and the full Result if one was returned. Say what you expected and whether it reproduces with the same inputs, and share a minimal redistributable fixture when possible. Review paths, coordinates, credentials, and source licenses before attaching files to a public issue, and use the security policy for vulnerabilities. Keep a reproducible run explains what to retain.


Concurrent stream queries


Use vigo stream --city ./city --workers 2 < requests.ndjson for a bounded resident worker pool. The default is one worker; requests accept one through four, capped by CPU and resident-memory capacity (two CPUs and 6 GiB per worker). Results and query errors retain input order. Each worker loads its own City and caches; no more than one response per worker is buffered. RAYON_NUM_THREADS controls threads within each Rust process, separately from the number of concurrent requests. For performance comparisons, keep worker count, thread count, City, cache policy and output options identical.


Detailed analytical Matrix streams with includeJourneys: true and includeGeometry: false return every timed leg, trip and stop reference, including boarding/alighting sequences and headway assumptions when present. They omit Studio display diagnostics and intermediate-stop presentation records. Set journeyFormat: "full" in the stream request for that additional metadata; includeGeometry: true also selects full materialization. This preserves the lightweight non-geometric Matrix contract used by the Python wrapper.


Engine and HTTP service


SymptomCheck and next action
Executable cannot runMatch OS/CPU target; on macOS/Linux retain executable permissions
--city or VIGO_CITY is requiredSet a prepared City directory, including for Compare
Expected a prepared vigo.city.v1 CityPoint to the compiler's complete output with network.json
Missing/stale access or CCH artifactRebuild/copy the whole City using a compatible compiler; do not mix artifacts from different builds
Unexpected SQLite WALComplete/checkpoint the source build and copy a consistent immutable City
Unknown stop IDUse exact scoped IDs from the active City; do not use display names
Route blockedCheck service date/clock, active calendar, direction, endpoint access, transfer cap/buffer, and walk limit
Empty or small ReachCheck largest cutoff, service availability, walk budget, raster extent, and street coverage; distinguish null from zero
Bad comparison gridRecompute both queries with identical explicit bounds and raster size; preserve other experimental settings
Realtime not changing the routeInspect diagnostic rejection counts, source time, static trip identity/date, and effective predictions
HTTP 401Set matching VIGO_API_TOKEN; send exactly one Bearer header
HTTP 503Read readiness; reduce concurrent work/queue pressure or add measured capacity
HTTP 504Inspect worker logs; reduce matrix size, geometry, raster detail, or split jobs before increasing deadlines
Browser request failsCheck same-origin/proxy configuration; native service does not implement CORS
Unsupported request fieldCheck this manual or the OpenAPI document; Studio's internal fields and compiler-only flags are not interchangeable
High memoryCity size, worker replication, Rayon threads, concurrent request bodies, and detailed results all contribute


Do not use repeated cached-query timing as a cold-start measurement. disableCache leaves loaded City data, prepared artifacts, OS page cache, and other resident state in place. Measure invocation-to-result or client request-to-response explicitly when reporting those boundaries.

Validation and compatibility
2 min readSource
On this page
Supported operationsPlatform and build recordsRun the checksUpdate the documentation
Use vigo capabilities to inspect the executable you are running. The standalone interface has its own request and response schemas; the table below describes its supported operations.


Supported operations


OperationModes and coverage
Route and MatrixTransit, walk, and drive; depart-at and arrive-by
ReachTransit, walk, and drive; driving uses a fixed grid with polygons and contours, without pedestrian street evidence
ScenariosReach with exclusions, explicit schedules, or compiled overlays
Realtime transitRoute, Matrix and Reach; supplied or polled, with Service Alerts
Supplied trafficDrive Route and Matrix
Saved comparisonReach surfaces


City compilation, Studio/Python response envelopes, fare annotations, fare optimization, and Studio route-preference presentation are outside the standalone interface. Prepare editor branches and automatic retiming as explicit schedules or overlays before querying. Native Pareto operations are available separately.


Platform and build records


The packaged test record reports the macOS ARM64 run. CI defines runtime checks for Linux x64/ARM64, macOS ARM64, and Windows x64; use the completed results for the exact build and target you deploy. Linux containers and Windows binaries were not executed in the recorded local audit. The Docker and systemd examples are deployment recipes, not additional test results.


manifest.json records the target, source commit, uncommitted-change flag, source digest, and file hashes. Packages built from uncommitted source are marked dirty: true and remain development artifacts. Keep the manifest with deployments so a result can be traced to its executable and source.


Run the checks


The adapter tests use public synthetic GTFS/OSM fixtures and compare outputs with the existing public CLI. Separate graph and timetable oracles check the shared kernels. These tests cover modeled routing behavior; source-feed completeness, field arrival accuracy, station accessibility, and deployment capacity require their own validation.


Shell
cargo test --manifest-path crates/vigo-runtime/Cargo.toml \
  --no-default-features --features standalone
cargo clippy --manifest-path crates/vigo-runtime/Cargo.toml \
  --no-default-features --features standalone --all-targets -- -D warnings
VIGO_STANDALONE_PATH=/absolute/path/to/vigo npm run check:standalone
python3 test/check-standalone-package.py /absolute/path/to/package.tar.gz
npm run docs:standalone
npm run check:standalone-docs


The documentation check verifies the generated guide and specification, links and contracts, and the executable JSON examples. Packaging validates every archive member and payload hash and reruns the adapter suites against the extracted binary. Node/Python are used for development validation only.


Update the documentation


For maintenance, edit this Markdown source. npm run docs:standalone regenerates the OpenAPI document and the native field reference from the Rust public structs, and npm run docs:build rebuilds the guide that the executable embeds. Check generated files before packaging so the embedded documentation describes the same executable.

Operate/Compatibility and validation
Engine audit record
4 min readSource
On this page
Corrected behaviorPublic validationOctober 4 follow-upRemaining compatibility boundaries
The standalone adapter uses VIGO's existing Rust timetable, street, driving, shape-alignment, and surface kernels. This audit corrected differences in the surrounding request handling, result materialization, realtime preparation, and deployment behavior. The supported operations now pass the public-fixture checks below. This is a development build, not a claim of complete Studio compatibility or production capacity.


Corrected behavior


AreaCorrection and retained regression evidence
Station selectionSelecting a station or child platform includes prepared station members. Map selections use coordinates. Differential routes cover parent and sibling platforms in both time directions.
WalkingDirect walking uses physical distance/speed. Transit access retains configured padding/overhead. Query walking speed reaches both Reach access and its surface. Tests use two City access policies and three walking speeds.
Route evidenceResults retain active stop sequences, route metadata, source-aligned GTFS shapes, and ride/walk/wait totals. Missing shapes and unverified walking geometry carry explicit provenance. Tests compare selected trips, stops, and geometry with the existing CLI.
RealtimeFreshness, trip identity, duplicates, cancellations, inferred terminal sequences, skipped calls, NO_DATA, and invalid predictions follow scheduled fallback semantics with diagnostics. Cached predictions expire; a source-clock crossing invalidates omitted-prefix fallback. A separate Rust test verifies removal of past-prefix boarding opportunities.
TrafficCache identities bind actual raw edge weights, even when a caller reuses its snapshot key. A two-query regression changes weights without changing the caller key.
ScenariosFrequency timing follows the selected time model, defaults match the public interface, and reverse directions charge added-stop dwell at the correct stop. Tests cover exclusions, distance estimates, supplied runtimes, and frequency replacement. Explicit scheduled-trip offsets and permissions are exercised separately.
Input and outputConflicting clocks, malformed fields, irrelevant CLI flags, invalid grids, unsafe CCH members, and oversized inputs are rejected. Saved JSON replaces its target atomically and preserves existing permissions.
HTTP lifecycleConnections, headers, bodies, query queue, and responses are bounded. Header/body deadlines cannot be extended by sending small chunks. Slow bodies do not occupy the query worker. A deadline kills and reaps the worker, including when a full input pipe blocks dispatch. Idle crashes restart without needing a query.
PackagingA fresh allowlisted directory prevents old output files from entering archives. The manifest hashes every payload file and the Rust source inputs; prior output is retained separately. The archive gate validates paths, member types, hashes, and the extracted executable.


Public validation


Observed locally on macOS ARM64 with Rust 1.97.1 and Node 24.18. Node builds synthetic Cities and runs the comparison interface; standalone queries run with an empty PATH and no Node runtime access.


CheckObserved result
test/check-standalone-parity.mjs276 cases passed against the existing public CLI
test/check-standalone.mjs64 queries/checks passed, including immutable City contents and authenticated HTTP
test/check-standalone-http.mjs18 checks passed, including malformed framing, slow-body timeout, capacity, SIGSTOP, full stdin pipe, worker reaping, and idle-crash recovery
Standalone Cargo unit tests19 passed, including raster holes/disconnected components and realtime past-prefix behavior
Default Node-feature Cargo unit tests17 passed
ClippyBoth default and standalone features passed with warnings denied
Existing kernel suitesNative routing, native matrices, and Reach engine checks passed
test/check-routing-accuracy.mjsPassed the existing synthetic independent-oracle checks for streets, driving, timetable queries, matrices, witnesses, and calendars


The differential suite covers two walking-access policies, both time directions, stop and coordinate endpoints, zero/one-transfer constraints, parent stations, sibling platforms, direct-walk policy, calendar additions/removals, matrices, scenario surfaces, realtime fallback, and source geometry. Route/Matrix time comparisons allow the existing interface's 0.001-minute presentation precision. Reach cells allow 0.00051 minutes because the existing adapter rounds transit seeds before surface construction; null/reachable classification must match exactly.


Agreement between adapters does not independently validate their shared kernels. The existing accuracy suite has separate graph and raw-GTFS enumeration oracles, but those remain synthetic tests. No real-world ETA, source-feed completeness, physical station connectivity, fare eligibility, throughput, or memory-capacity claim follows from these results.


To reproduce in a development checkout, build the existing public CLI and native addon, build the standalone executable, and run npm run check:standalone with VIGO_STANDALONE_PATH set to it. Package with python3 scripts/package-standalone.py; then run python3 test/check-standalone-package.py ARCHIVE.tar.gz. That gate reruns all three adapter suites against the extracted binary. Node and Python are development tools; neither ships in the runtime payload. POSIX worker-stop/crash injection is skipped on Windows.


October 4 follow-up


The table above records the original October 3 audit. An October 4 macOS ARM64 follow-up (Rust 1.97.1, Node 26.7.0 as the fixture/compiler host) passed 69 standalone checks, 63 prepared-data checks, 332 differential/regression cases, 18 HTTP lifecycle checks, 42 documentation/HTTP checks, and 23 standalone Cargo tests. Standalone Clippy passed with warnings denied. The additional cases compare current and expired access witnesses in both time directions, repeated matrix endpoints, cached/uncached requests, and two City access policies. They also verify that missing transit access skips the timetable scan without suppressing a requested direct-walk result. Public fixtures remain synthetic; these counts do not establish production capacity or field accuracy.


Remaining compatibility boundaries


  • City preparation from raw GTFS/OSM remains the existing compiler. The executable consumes an immutable prepared City.
  • JSON uses the documented standalone schema. Studio/Python envelope compatibility, fare annotations, and Studio route-preference presentation are not implemented.
  • Scenario editor branch selection and automatic retiming remain preparation steps. Supply explicit scheduled trips or compiled overlays for those changes.
  • Realtime transit applies to Route; current public CLI and standalone Matrix/Reach do not provide realtime transit queries.
  • Saved-result comparison currently accepts Reach surfaces. It verifies City revision and grid compatibility, not every experimental setting.
  • The executable and container recipe are generic, but this local audit did not execute Linux containers or Windows binaries. Release CI is configured to check the corresponding targets. Public hosting and capacity testing remain deployment work.


The package manifest reports source dirty state. A dirty checkout artifact remains a development artifact even when its local checks pass. Nothing in this audit publishes or releases it.

On this page
Start with a working exampleThree questions, one CityRead the result correctlyKeep repeated work efficientReference and support
VIGO Python 1.0.0rc2 gives scripts and notebooks a small set of objects for transport analysis. Build or open a City, run Route, Matrix, or Reach, and retain the Result. Reuse one open City for repeated work.


Start with a working example


  • Your first queryInstall the package, select Engine 1.0, and route using a prepared City.
  • Build a CityTurn local GTFS and OSM inputs into a reusable network.
  • Calculate a matrixEvaluate many origins and destinations together, with optional journeys.
  • Compare a service changeRun baseline and Scenario queries on the same City.


Three questions, one City


Python
import vigo

with vigo.open("./boston") as city:
    result = city.route(
        [-71.11902, 42.37334],
        [-71.05524, 42.35227],
        depart_at="08:00",
        service_date="2026-10-05",
    )
    if result.status == "ready":
        print(result.duration_minutes)


This example requires a City covering central Boston and a feed active on the chosen date. Coordinates are [longitude, latitude]. Transit may choose a direct walk; set require_transit_ride=True when a boarding is required.


QueryAnswerReference
RouteA journey between ordered placesRoute
MatrixTravel times for pairs of placesMatrix
ReachReachable streets and areas within a time budgetReach


Read the result correctly


Python uses ready and blocked Result statuses and minute-valued travel times. A completed Matrix can contain blocked rows. Invalid inputs and execution failures raise exceptions. Results and exports explains each field and the comparison rules.


The public Engine CLI and HTTP schemas use seconds and different status names. Use Python's documented Result properties in Python applications.


Keep repeated work efficient


Use a context manager, retain the open City, and request Matrix journeys or geometry only when needed. Install the optional speed extra for accelerated response decoding. Use result.iter_rows() to copy only consumed rows. Runtime and performance explains process reuse, timing, and resource lifetime.


Reference and support

Your first Python query
VIGO Python 1.0.0rc22 min readSource
On this page
1. Install2. Prepare the City3. Run a journey query4. Read and reuse the answer
Install VIGO Python 1.0.0rc2, select Engine 1.0, and open a prepared City. The example below asks for a journey from Harvard Square to South Station.


1. Install


For a packaged installation, download the VIGO-Python-… ZIP matching your OS and CPU from the VIGO releases page and unzip it. It contains the wheel, INSTALL.txt, and the runtime manifest. Replace the filename below with the unzipped wheel:


Shell
python -m pip install "/path/to/vigo-1.0.0rc2-py3-none-PLATFORM.whl[speed]"


Platform wheels include Node, the headless CLI bundle, and the Rust kernel. The optional speed extra adds accelerated JSON decoding. Omit the extra for the dependency-free Python package; the packaged Engine is still included. Python 3.10 or newer is required.


From a source checkout, install the wrapper and select a separately built Engine:


Shell
python -m pip install -e ".[speed]"
export VIGO_RUNTIME=/path/to/headless-runtime


VIGO_RUNTIME can name a complete headless directory or a built vigo.mjs file. A source .mjs needs system Node and its matching native kernel. See runtime selection for complete layouts and Windows usage.


2. Prepare the City


A City is a prepared directory built once from a static GTFS ZIP and an OpenStreetMap .osm.pbf. The Engine Boston tutorial lists where to download both. Save this as build.py and run it once:


Python
import vigo

with vigo.build(
    "./boston",
    gtfs="./data/MBTA_GTFS.zip",
    osm="./data/massachusetts-latest.osm.pbf",
) as city:
    print(city.name, city.revision_id)
    print("timetable covers", city.service_period())


In a terminal or notebook, Build prints each stage and the elapsed time; a Boston build takes a few minutes. Missing input files are reported before anything starts. Build refuses to overwrite an existing City unless you pass replace=True.


Build once; reopen the saved City with vigo.open() in later sessions. Do not call Build inside a query loop. Keep the entire directory, including its timetable and street files. If a prepared City predates the supported format, rebuild it from its original inputs into a new directory.


3. Run a journey query


Save this as route.py. The example requires Boston street coverage and a timetable active on October 5, 2026, as in the Engine tutorial. With another feed download, pick a date inside city.service_period().


Python
import vigo

with vigo.open("./boston") as city:
    result = city.route(
        [-71.11902, 42.37334],
        [-71.05524, 42.35227],
        depart_at="08:00",
        service_date="2026-10-05",
        max_walk_km=1.2,
        require_transit_ride=True,
    )
    if result.status == "ready":
        print(f"Journey: {result.duration_minutes:.1f} minutes")
        for leg in result.legs:
            print(leg["type"])
    else:
        print("No journey under the supplied constraints.")
    result.export("route-result.json")


Run it with the same interpreter used for installation:


Shell
python route.py


The first query starts the resident process and opens the required data. Further queries in the same with block reuse that process. Exiting the block releases it; returned Results remain usable.


4. Read and reuse the answer


duration_minutes is the selected journey duration. legs contains its timed steps and available geometry. Inspect warnings before using a path in a passenger-facing application. A blocked Result is a valid no-journey outcome; VigoError reports a failed operation.


Next, try arrive-by routing, a travel-time matrix, or walking and transit Reach. The batch workflow keeps failures separate from valid blocked results.

VIGO concepts in Python
VIGO Python 1.0.0rc24 min readSource
On this page
CityScenarioQueryRouteMatrixReachResultTimePython
VIGO has four first-class concepts and three Query families. Build or open a City, optionally apply a Scenario, then retain the Result of a Query.


City -> Route | Matrix | Reach -> Result
  ^
optional Scenario


City


A City is a compiled mobility model built from GTFS and OSM. Its directory is one atomic unit containing the timetable, street model, and the data needed to open them quickly.


A named City may be rebuilt over time. Each build is an immutable revision. A Result records the revision it used.


city.revision_id identifies the build. city.built_at records when it was created. city.sources records its GTFS and OSM inputs. Moving the complete City directory does not change that identity.


Scenario


A Scenario is an immutable set of changes applied to exactly one City revision.


The shared VIGO model can describe:


  • proposed transit service changes;
  • one live transit state;
  • one supplied traffic state.


Query choices such as a walking limit, departure time, or time cutoff are not Scenario changes. A complete alternative GTFS source is another City revision, not a Scenario. Map geometry used to draw an edit is presentation data, not a transport change by itself.


VIGO checks a selected combination before running it. It never drops an unsupported change and quietly returns the unchanged City.


Python supports planned service changes in Reach and supplied traffic in Drive Route/Matrix. Python live-transit Scenarios, realtime transit Matrix, and realtime Reach are unsupported. Supplied traffic uses the shared native driving kernel and requires an engine that advertises that capability.


city.supports(query) and scenario.supports(query) return a Support value with a reason and available alternative when the selected context cannot execute a combination. This is not a complete data-validation pass; execution still checks points, dates, and runtime inputs. See the Python support table.


Query


VIGO has exactly three Query families.


Route


Find and explain travel between ordered points. Transport mode, depart-at, arrive-by, departure windows, waypoints, and batch requests are Route options.


Depart-at minimizes arrival time, then boardings, then walking. Arrive-by maximizes departure time, then minimizes boardings and walking among journeys arriving by the deadline, then actual arrival.


Matrix


Compute scalar travel time between one or more origins and destinations.


Both depart-at and arrive-by accept up to 100,000 pairs. Fixed departures share one forward scan per unique origin; fixed arrival deadlines share one reverse scan per unique destination. Arrive-by duration runs from the latest departure to the deadline, including destination waiting.


Reach


Compute where the represented network can travel within stated time limits. A Reach Result may be viewed as contours or reached streets.


Depart-at Reach spreads from an origin. Arrive-by Reach gathers toward a destination: it maps where a traveler can leave from and still arrive by a deadline, such as the homes that can reach a school by 08:30.


Reach is not Accessibility. Accessibility requires opportunities such as jobs, population, schools, or healthcare in addition to travel impedance.


Result


A Result is the immutable answer to one Query. Every Result exposes:


  • status;
  • Query inputs;
  • warnings;
  • timing;
  • City revision and Scenario name;
  • export methods.


Compare is an action on two compatible Results. It is not a fourth Query family.


Result status is only ready or blocked. A completed Matrix is ready even when individual rows are blocked. Python-side query validation raises InvalidQuery; unsupported combinations raise UnsupportedQuery; runtime validation and execution failures raise VigoError. Background work separately reports queued, running, ready, cancelled, or error through Job.status.


Compare uses retained values and checks family-specific structure; the caller must align dates, points, modes, and other study assumptions. A valid numerical difference does not establish that two Results answer the same question. See Results for comparison and evidence boundaries.


Time


VIGO keeps these durations separate:


  • Build: GTFS and OSM become a City.
  • Open: a City revision becomes ready for queries.
  • Compute: the selected Query runs.
  • End to end: caller submission through complete Result.


Repeated Route calls may reuse one open process. The answer is still computed for every call.


The wrapper's timing["endToEndMs"] ends before Result construction and export. Use an outer timer for the complete Python operation; see runtime measurement.


Python


Python
import vigo

with vigo.open("./city") as city:
    route = city.route("A", "B", depart_at="08:00", service_date="2026-09-04")
    matrix = city.matrix({"a": "A"}, {"b": "B"}, depart_at="08:00", service_date="2026-09-04")
    reach = city.reach("A", depart_at="08:00", service_date="2026-09-04")


The VIGO command line uses the same nouns: vigo build, vigo inspect, vigo route, vigo matrix, vigo reach, and vigo compare.


vigo capabilities reports the public API version and supported combinations. VIGO Python V1 supports the VIGO V1 engine with API 1.0, capability schema v3, and trace output. Runtime selection rejects other API versions and capability schemas.


Route and Matrix accept max_transfers=0 for at most one boarding, max_transfers=1 for at most two, and so on through 31. Omit the option (or use None) for no additional cap. It applies to both depart_at and arrive_by and all Matrix shapes. A finite cap with ordered transit waypoints is currently unsupported.
